comments.text: The base of two zero-page clears through STA $00,X: $14C8, before each load, zeroes $02-$FF, and stage_start clears $0B-$10. The processor port's direction register itself is never written.
The 6510's port, choosing the memory map: start, irq_install, ram_and_io ($35), kernal_open_file ($36), stage_start and memory_swap write it.
timing_check's frame count: timing_check_arm sets it, timing_check counts it down between two raster interrupts.
The CIA timer reading timing_check takes, low byte; read again at $CF6B to measure the frame.
The CIA timer reading timing_check takes, high byte.
Where irq_save keeps A during a raster interrupt; irq_restore gives it back.
Where irq_save keeps X; irq_restore gives it back.

The VSP column: how many characters the playfield is shifted by raster_vsp's delayed DMA, moved on by irq_scroll as the landscape scrolls.

The fine scroll (0-7) for $D016, kept by irq_scroll and written at the top of the playfield by raster_vsp; player_find_cell and shot_hits_wall subtract it to find a sprite's character column; get_ready clears it.
Work byte: the object being tested (object_collisions, from $12DF), and the low byte of a screen pointer ($39/$3A) for scroll_finish_column and the panel; many routines borrow it.
Work byte: the high byte of the screen pointer at $39, and in object_collisions the slot of the object whose sprite is tested.
Work byte: the bottom of the collision box (player_box_y, shot_box), the low byte of the destination pointer ($3B/$3C) in scroll_draw_column and scroll_finish_column, and object_spawn's record byte.
Work byte: the top of the collision box, and the high byte of the pointer at $3B.
Work byte: the high bit of the box's right edge ($3F) in player_box_x and object_collisions, and scroll_draw_column's character count.
Work byte: the high bit of the box's left edge, an object's bit mask in object_collisions ($12E9), and the low byte of the colour RAM pointer ($3E/$3F) for put_colour.
Work byte: the right edge of the collision box (x + 16 for Clyde), and the high byte of the colour pointer at $3E.
Work byte: the left edge of the collision box (x - 15 for Clyde), and scroll_draw_column's row counter.
Work byte: object_collisions' high-bit test, and the low byte of the movement script pointer ($41/$42) in move_objects.
Work byte: where object_collisions' box lies against x position 256, ($3D shifted left) exclusive-or $3E, worked out as it starts; move_objects uses it as the high byte of the script pointer at $41.
shot_collisions' shot (X), kept for shot_spent.
The x high bit of Clyde or the shot, which player_box_x and shot_box return in A and their callers store here for object_collisions.
Clyde's (or the shot's) x position, kept by player_box_x and shot_box for object_collisions' left-of-centre test.
object_collisions' second-pass flag for double-height sprites: cleared, then set when the box is tested again 15 lines lower.
The first world's first ambient-sound range, its first scroll column, from the table at $CFBF (world1_ranges).
The first range's last column, $0047 plus 15: fifteen columns for the fifteen sound values at $CFC4.
The second range's first scroll column, from the table at $CFC1 (world1_ranges).
The second range's last column, $0049 plus 15, matching the fifteen values at $CFD3.

Work byte of shot_hit_object's scoring at $3EA8.
Low byte of the pointer shot_hits_wall uses to read the character under a shot.
High byte of the pointer at $4E.
Set by world1_ranges for the first world's level code, from its table at $CFBC.
Set by world1_ranges for the first world's level code, with $51.
Low byte of the first pointer of tablet_swap_step ($53/$54), set by tablet_close_setup.
High byte of tablet_swap_step's first pointer; also the low byte of rotate_bytes' list pointer ($54/$55).
Low byte of tablet_swap_step's second pointer ($55/$56), and the high byte of rotate_bytes' list pointer.
High byte of tablet_swap_step's second pointer, and rotate_bytes' index into its list.
Low byte of memory_swap's first pointer ($7E/$7F); also ride_parent's object and hiscore_check's place.
High byte of memory_swap's first pointer, moved on a page at a time; move_objects keeps the object number here as well.
Low byte of memory_swap's second pointer ($80/$81).
High byte of memory_swap's second pointer.

ride_parent's copy of the carrying object's x position, from obj_xy.
ride_parent's copy of the carrying object's y position; hiscore_check keeps four times the place it found here.

ride_parent: the riding object's band (Y from slot_group), which picks its byte of obj_x_msb.
ride_parent: the riding object's place in its band (X from slot_group), which picks its bit.
ride_parent: the riding object's ninth x bit, copied from the carrying object's before the offset is added; an offset that carries flips it ($C727).
Low byte of the address of Clyde's screen character, left by player_find_cell; player_control and the level's routines read the cells around him through ($8A),Y.
High byte of the address at $8A.
Low byte of the pointer to the spawn record object_spawn is reading ($8E/$8F).
High byte of the spawn record pointer.
The KERNAL's status byte (ST): kernal_open_file clears it and tests it for a missing drive or file.
fast_loader's bit counter.
fast_loader's received byte, handed on to load_byte.
The byte nothing reads: the BIT $00A9 instructions at $0520, $1B35 and $21A3 are there only to hide an LDA #$00 in their operand from the other path.
The KERNAL's end-of-load address low byte; kernal_open_file stores the first byte read from the file here.
The KERNAL's secondary address: kernal_open_file sets $60 for the file's channel; fast_loader reads it.
The KERNAL's current device number (8), read for LISTEN and TALK and by drive_command_open and fast_loader.

Pointers to the tile data of the six map rows, two bytes each ($C6-$D1), set by scroll_column and read by scroll_draw_column through ($C6),Y, ($C8),Y ... ($D0),Y; get_ready and get_ready_strip also use $C6.

The second map row's tile pointer; raster_ready_top's counter on the Get Ready screen.
High byte of the second row's tile pointer; rotate_slow's counter.

High byte of the third row's tile pointer; raster_ready_icons' second counter.
The fourth map row's tile pointer.
The fifth map row's tile pointer.
The sixth map row's tile pointer.
Low byte of the pointer through which the panel's face graphic is copied at $2A65.
High byte of the pointer at $D2.
The 15 objects' x movement script pointers, low bytes, set by object_spawn, hit_response_path and object_kill; move_objects reads the script through them ($41/$42).
The 15 objects' x movement script pointers, high bytes (see $00D9); zero means the object has no x script.
Low byte of the music data pointer of the voice being played ($FC/$FD), saved per voice in music_ptr_lo/hi.
High byte of the music data pointer.
The SID register offset of the voice being played (0, 7 or 14); fast_loader borrows it as a counter.
music_next_note's work byte (the note length's high part, and the loop count in music_cmd_loop and music_cmd_call).

Object table, one byte for each of the 15 objects (cleared when an object dies). Before the first stage starts the first bytes hold the BASIC line of the game file's loader ("SYS 5632"), which nothing reads.
The 15 objects' read positions in their y movement scripts (move_object_y), set by object_spawn and object_kill.
The 15 objects' read positions in their animation scripts (animate_objects), set by object_spawn and object_set_type.
The 15 objects' read positions in their colour cycles (object_colours), set by object_spawn and object_kill.

The 15 objects' active flags: object_spawn sets one, and objects_scroll, object_collisions, shot_hit_object, object_flash and move_objects skip an object whose flag is zero. The 49 bytes after the table, to $027B, are zeros nothing refers to.

The KERNAL's vectors, $0300-$0333, as the KERNAL left them. The engine changes the IRQ vector $0314 (irq_install) and the NMI vector $0318 (start); the KERNAL reaches the rest through its own routines.
KERNAL IRQ vector, low byte; irq_install points it at irq_entry.
KERNAL IRQ vector, high byte.
KERNAL NMI vector; start sets its low byte to $C1, pointing it at the RTI at $FEC1 in the KERNAL ROM.
Music-on flag: music_frame runs the player only while it is set; music_init sets it and music_stop clears it.

Music player, one tick per frame for the three voices. A speed counter ($0898 against $0897) decides on which frames the voices read new commands; a global filter sweep adds $08B4/$08B5 to the shadow cutoff $095A/$095B every frame. For each voice (X = 2 down to 0, SID register offset from $093B) it reads two-byte commands at the voice's data pointer ($0938/$0935): a first byte below $25 picks a command from the jump table at $095E/$0983 (the JSR at $03CD is rewritten to point at it), with the second byte in A; otherwise the voice's note timer, effects (portamento $0765, vibrato $06A0, waveform choice, arpeggio $0671, pulse sweep $061B) and gate are updated in the shadow registers at $0945.
Operand of the JSR at $03CD: the address of the music command handler, written from the jump tables each time a command is read.

High byte of the handler address in the JSR at $03CD (the low byte is $03CE), both written from music_cmd_lo and music_cmd_hi. After the handler the loop reads the next item (music_advance). Once a note is reached, the voice's frame work runs from $03D5: portamento once the note is older than music_porta_delay, vibrato when it has a depth, and the attack waveform: values 1 to 5 put waveform music_waveforms_m1[value] in the voice's control register for the first music_attack_len frames of the note; values 6 and up alternate waveform value - 5 with the note's own control byte (music_ctrl) on every other step.

The first address memory_wipe clears: its STA at $AF72 starts here and climbs. In music_update this is where attack values 6 and up subtract 5 to pick their waveform; from $0410 the 1-5 case tests the note's age against music_attack_len, the chosen control byte goes to the voice's shadow register at $0949, then the arpeggio and pulse sweep run when set, the note timer counts down on the music's tick, the voice's data pointer ($FC/$FD) is saved to music_ptr_lo/hi, and the loop moves to the next voice.
Operand of the CPX at $0455: where music_update's voice loop stops. 0 plays all three voices (music_hooks_all); music_hooks_ingame sets 2, so that only the third voice is played during a level.
Counts down the current note's length ($0932/$08E7, a 16-bit count per voice); near the end it clears the gate bit in the voice's shadow control register, and at zero it falls into music_next_note.

Starts the next note of a voice: clears the voice's effect counters, reloads ADSR and pulse width from the voice's instrument settings ($090B, $0902, $0908), reads the note byte (zero is a rest), converts it with music_note_freq (adding the transpose and an optional second interval for arpeggio), stores the frequency in the shadow registers and the voice's state, then reads the length byte. A note byte of $19 takes a further length byte.

Starts the tune whose header $FC/$FD points at. Clears the player's 155 bytes of state ($0896-$0930), gives each voice a release point of 2, a note length of 1 and a vibrato period of 1, and sets the tempo $0897 to 1. Keeps the header address in $093E/$093F as the base for section calls. Voice 1's data starts right after the four-byte header; the header holds two 16-bit offsets, relative to that point, for voices 2 and 3. Then silences the shadow registers, runs two ticks and sets the music-on flag $0334.
Clears the music-on flag $0334, then (entered at $058E) clears the 24 shadow SID registers $0945-$095C and the volume register $D418.
Clears the shadow SID registers $0945-$095C and the SID's volume and filter register.
Music command: repeat a section. Counts the voice's loop counter ($0911,X) up; until it reaches the count in A, jumps the data pointer back to the address saved by music_cmd_loop_mark.

Music command: mark the start of a repeated section, saving the voice's data pointer in $0917/$091D and clearing its loop counter. $05CA and $05D2 are the same pair of commands for a second, nested loop level (offset by three voices).

Music commands that each store A into one voice setting: $05D8 transpose (music_transpose, $08F9); $05DC, for values below 100, the attack waveform's length in frames (music_attack_len, $08AE, which the player compares with the note's age), and for 100 and more the release point less 100 (music_release, $08A5); $05EA, for values below 99, the attack waveform (music_attack_wave, $08AB), and for 99 and more, less 100, the voice whose notes drive the filter (music_filter_voice, $0896); $05F8 pulse sweep limits ($08F3 high nibble, $08F6 low nibble), $0607 vibrato period ($092F), $060B filter resonance and routing ($095C), $060F filter start ($08B6), $0613 adds A to the volume and filter mode ($095D).
Sweeps a voice's pulse width (shadow $0947/$0948) up and down by the step in $090E between the limits held in $08F3 and $08F6, turning at each.
Music command: sets the voice's control (waveform and gate) byte $0905.
Arpeggio, mode 1: on alternate frames ($08E1 bit 0) puts the note's second frequency ($08BA/$08BD) or its own frequency into the shadow registers.
Vibrato: after a delay ($08C9), moves the frequency up or down by the depth $08C6 each frame through music_freq_up/down, changing direction every $092F frames in a four-step cycle ($08ED).

Music commands that store A into a setting: $06D8 arpeggio interval ($08D5), $06DC filter sweep step (high five bits to $08B5, low three to $08B4), $06EA tempo ($0897), $06EE second-note interval ($08D2), $06F2 adds A to the transpose ($08F9), $06FA vibrato delay ($08CC).
Music command 33: sets the voice's vibrato delay ($08CC), reached through music_cmd_lo/hi like the other commands.
Music command: return from a called section, restoring the data pointer saved by music_cmd_call ($0923/$0929) and the outer saved one.
Music command: fine tune added to every note's frequency ($08E4).
Adds the vibrato depth $08C6 to the voice's 16-bit frequency ($0899/$089C) and writes it to the shadow registers; $0730 subtracts it.
Subtracts the vibrato depth from the voice's frequency and writes it to the shadow registers (the other half of music_freq_up).
Converts a note number (bits 0-6, plus the voice's transpose $08F9) to a SID frequency from the table at $09A8, adds the fine tune $08E4, and returns it in A (low) and Y (high).
Music command: high byte of the portamento step ($08FF); $088E sets the low byte ($08FC).

Portamento: mode 1 glides the frequency towards the target note ($08BA/$08BD) from either side and stops on it, mode 3 glides down, mode 2 (never reached in the recorded play) glides up. Steps are $08FC/$08FF.
Music command: pulse-width sweep step ($090E).
Moves the voice's data pointer $FC/$FD on by one two-byte command.
Starts a tune: Y and X are the low and high bytes of its header. Turns the player off while music_init sets it up.

Music commands that store A into one voice setting: $0810 portamento delay ($08C0), $0814 vibrato depth ($08C6), $0818 portamento mode ($08B7), $081C arpeggio mode ($08A8), $0820 step rate ($08B1), $0824 attack/decay ($090B), $0828 volume and filter mode ($095D), $0867 sustain/release ($0902), $0892 pulse width high byte ($0908).
Music command 6: sets the voice's step rate for the arpeggio and three-step cycle ($08B1), reached through music_cmd_lo/hi.
Music command: sets the attack and decay of the voice's notes ($090B), reached through the command tables; $0828 is the next one, which sets the volume (music_volume).
Music command: converts A to a frequency and makes it the portamento target ($08BD/$08BA).

Music command: call a section. Saves the return pointer (two levels, $0923/$0929 and $0926/$092C), then jumps the voice's data pointer to the tune base plus the 16-bit offset given by A and the next byte.
Music command: end of tune. Stops the music and drops the player's two return addresses, so the frame's update ends there.
Called every frame from the interrupt: when the music-on flag $0334 is set, runs music_update and copies the 25 shadow registers $0945-$095D to the SID at $D400-$D418.
Runs music_update and copies the shadow registers to the SID, without checking the music-on flag (music_init calls it twice).
Operand of the LDY at $087B: the first shadow register music_frame copies to the SID ($18, counting down).

Operand of the CPY at $0886: the shadow register below which copying stops. 0 copies down to $D400 (all voices); during a level it is $0E, so only the third voice's and the filter and volume registers are written.
RTS of the last command handler. music_init addresses $0895,Y with Y from 155 down to 1, so this is the base of the state it clears ($0896-$0930), not a target of its own.
The voice (0-2) whose every new note restarts the filter sweep: the cutoff is reset from $08B6 when that voice starts a note. Set by a music command ($05EA, values above 98).
Tempo: the number of frames between the frames on which the voices read new commands.
Frame counter for the tempo; the voices read commands on the frame it wraps to zero.
Current frequency of each voice, low byte (three bytes, one per voice; the high bytes are at $089C).
Current frequency of each voice, high byte.
The note each voice is playing (zero for a rest).
Each voice's control byte (waveform and gate) for the current note, copied from $0905 when the note starts.
Release point of each voice: when the note's remaining length (low byte, high byte zero) falls below it, the gate bit is cleared.
Arpeggio mode of each voice (0 off); see music_arpeggio.

Attack waveform of each voice: 0 none, 1-5 a control byte from music_waveforms used for the first frames of each note ($08AE frames), then the note's own control byte. Values of 6 and more take the path at $0400, which no recorded tune reached.
Number of frames the attack waveform lasts at the start of each note (0: the whole note).
Frames per step of the arpeggio and the three-step cycle of each voice.
Filter sweep: added to the cutoff's low three bits each frame (set with $08B5 by music command $06DC).
Filter sweep: added to the cutoff's high byte each frame, with the carry from $08B4.
Filter cutoff (high byte) that the sweep restarts from on each note of the filter voice.

Portamento mode of each voice: 0 off, 1 glide to the target note, 2 up, 3 down (three bytes; $08B8 and $08B9 are the second and third voice's, also written by music_init's header loop through $08B8,X).
The second and third voices' portamento modes (see music_porta_mode), which music_init's header loop also writes.
Portamento target frequency of each voice, low byte; music_init's header loop also stores through $08BB,X (X from $7E) into the voice pointers.
The second and third voices' portamento targets, low bytes (see music_porta_lo), also written by music_init's header loop.
Portamento target frequency of each voice, high byte.
Frames after the start of a note before the portamento starts.
Frames since the voice's current note started (cleared at each note, counted each tick); compared with the portamento delay and the attack length.
Vibrato depth of each voice: the frequency step per frame (0 off).
Vibrato delay counter of each voice, reloaded from $08CC at each note.
Vibrato delay of each voice, in frames.
A counter of each voice stepping 0, 1, 2 every $08B1 frames, cleared at each note.
Glide interval of each voice: when not zero, each note glides towards the note this many semitones away (music_cmd_porta_target).
Arpeggio interval of each voice, the semitones of the second note (the code that uses it, at $04D0, is not reached in the recorded tunes).
The three voices' arpeggio notes, the frequency's low byte that music_arpeggio writes on the arpeggio's second step.
The three voices' arpeggio notes, high byte, set by music_next_note and written by music_arpeggio.
Frame counter of each voice towards the next arpeggio step ($08B1).
Arpeggio step counter of each voice; bit 0 picks which of the two frequencies plays.
Fine tune of each voice, added to every note's frequency.
Remaining length of the voice's note, high byte ($FF before the first note); the low byte is at $0932.
Vibrato frame counter of each voice, towards a change of direction every $092F frames.
Vibrato phase of each voice, a four-step cycle (up, down, down, up).
Pulse sweep direction of each voice.
Pulse sweep upper limit of each voice.
Pulse sweep lower limit of each voice.
Transpose of each voice, in semitones.
Portamento step of each voice, low byte.
Portamento step of each voice, high byte.
Sustain and release of each voice's notes.
Control byte (waveform) of each voice's notes, copied into the note at its start.
Pulse width (high byte) of each voice's notes.
Attack and decay of each voice's notes.
Pulse sweep step of each voice (0 off).
Repeat counters of each voice, two levels ($0911 and $0914).
Saved data pointer (low bytes) of each voice's repeated sections, two levels.
Saved data pointer (high bytes) of each voice's repeated sections, two levels.
Return pointers (low bytes) of each voice's called sections, two levels.
Second-level return pointers (low bytes) of each voice's called sections.
Return pointers (high bytes) of each voice's called sections.
Second-level return pointers (high bytes) of each voice's called sections.
Vibrato period of each voice: frames between changes of direction.
Remaining length of the voice's note, low byte (high byte $08E7).
Data pointer of each voice, high byte.
Data pointer of each voice, low byte.
SID register offsets of the three voices: 0, 7 and 14.
Address of the tune's header (low $093E, high $093F), the base for section calls.
High byte of the tune base; also the base of the waveform table, which music_update indexes as $093F,Y with Y from 1 to 5 (the table proper starts at $0940).
Control bytes chosen by a voice's waveform setting 1-5: pulse ($41), sawtooth ($21), triangle ($11), noise ($81), pulse and triangle ($51).
Shadow copy of the SID registers $D400-$D418, written by the player and copied out by music_frame each frame.
Shadow of voice 1's frequency high byte; with Y = 0, 7 or 14, the same register of each voice ($D401, $D408, $D40F).
Shadow of the voice's pulse width, low byte (indexed by the voice's register offset).
Shadow of the voice's pulse width, high byte.
Shadow of the voice's control register (waveform and gate).
Shadow of the voice's attack and decay.
Shadow of the voice's sustain and release; $0952 and $0959 are the second and third voices' (the shadow continues to $095D).
Shadow of the filter cutoff, low three bits ($D415).
Shadow of the filter cutoff, high byte ($D416).
Shadow of the filter resonance and voice routing ($D417).
Shadow of the filter mode and volume ($D418).
Low bytes of the 37 music command handlers, indexed by the command number minus one; the high bytes follow at $0983.
High bytes of the 37 music command handlers (see music_cmd_lo).
SID frequencies of 96 notes, eight octaves from C-0 ($0116) to B-7 ($F810), two bytes each, low byte first.
music_freq_table read from its second byte: music_note_freq takes each frequency's high byte at $09A9,Y (low byte at $09A8,Y), Y being twice the note; these 64 bytes are the table's first 32 entries.
music_freq_table from note 32 (G#-2) to note 95 (B-7), two bytes each, low byte first.

Sound effects, one tick per frame for three channels (Y = 2 down to 0, channel state at offsets 0, $1D and $3A of $0C1A): counts down each effect's length, sweeps its frequency and pulse width between limits, and every $0C2C frames switches between the effect's two sets of SID values; ends the effect and clears its priority ($125D) when the length runs out.
Operand of the LDY at $0A68: the number of the highest sound effect channel, 2 (three channels) or 1 when the in-game music has the third voice (sound_set_music_mode).
Operand of the LDY at $0A91: the channel being updated, saved by sfx_update at $0A6A.

One sound effect channel's tick (X = state offset, $FF = SID voice offset): length countdown, frequency sweep up, down or bouncing between two limits ($0C2B bits 0-3), second frequency sweep ($0C2B bits 4-7), pulse sweep, then writes frequency, pulse and control to the SID voice from one of the two parameter sets.
Operand of the LDA at $0B55: the frequency (high byte) at which a sweep restarts, written from the limits at $0B35.
Operand of the LDA at $0BC5: the restart frequency of the second sweep, written at $0BA5.

Sound effect channels' state, three blocks of 29 bytes ($0C1A, $0C37, $0C54), one per channel. The first 20 bytes are copied from the effect's definition by sfx_start: attack/decay, sustain/release, then the fields named below; the rest is working state. In the file as loaded these bytes hold leftover assembler text ("...HEX 5C5D5EB0...").
Sound effect channel: sustain and release (definition byte 1).
Sound effect channel: first frequency's lower limit, high byte (definition byte 2).
Sound effect channel: first frequency's upper limit, high byte (byte 3).
Sound effect channel: first frequency's sweep step, low byte (byte 4).
Sound effect channel: first frequency's sweep step, high byte (byte 5).
Sound effect channel: first parameter set's pulse width, high byte (byte 6); lowered by the pulse sweep.
Sound effect channel: flags (byte 7). Bit 0 sweeps the pulse width down by $0C27 each frame, bit 3 alternates between the two parameter sets every $0C2C frames.
Sound effect channel: second frequency's lower limit, high byte (byte 8).
Sound effect channel: second frequency's upper limit, high byte (byte 9).
Sound effect channel: second frequency's sweep step, low byte (byte 10).
Sound effect channel: second frequency's sweep step, high byte (byte 11).
Sound effect channel: second parameter set's pulse width, high byte (byte 12).
Sound effect channel: pulse sweep step (byte 13).
Sound effect channel: first parameter set's control byte (waveform and gate, byte 14).
Sound effect channel: second parameter set's control byte (byte 15).
Sound effect channel: length, low byte (byte 16); counted down each frame.

Sound effect channel: sweep modes (byte 17). Bits 0-1: first frequency still, up (1) or down (2 or 3); bits 2-3 what happens at the limit: 0 stop, 4 restart from the other limit, otherwise turn round. Bits 4-7: the same for the second frequency.
Sound effect channel: frames between switches of parameter set (byte 18).
Sound effect channel: length, high byte (byte 19); the effect ends when it passes zero.
Sound effect channel: first frequency, low byte (working state).
Sound effect channel: first frequency, high byte.
Sound effect channel: second frequency, low byte.
Sound effect channel: second frequency, high byte.
Sound effect channel: 1 while an effect plays.
Sound effect channel: which parameter set is playing (0 or 1).
Sound effect channel: first parameter set's pulse width, low byte.
Sound effect channel: second parameter set's pulse width, low byte.
Sound effect channel: frames left before the next switch of parameter set.
SID register offset of each sound effect channel's voice: 0, 7, 14.
Offset of each channel's state block in sfx_state: 0, $1D, $3A.
Offset of the last definition byte in each channel's state block ($13, $30, $4D); sfx_start copies the definition backwards from there.
Two bytes of $FF before the effect address table; nothing reads them.
Addresses of the 30 sound effect definitions, two bytes each, low byte first; each definition is 20 bytes from $0D62.
High bytes of the sound effect definitions' addresses (the table is read as words from $0C7C).
Clears the SID's voice registers, the six sound effect request bytes $1260-$1265, and sets the volume to 15.

Starts effect definition Y (an entry of sfx_effects) on channel X: copies its 20-byte definition (sfx_defs) into the channel's state, gates the SID voice off, sets attack, decay, sustain and release, and the starting frequencies of both parameter sets.
Operand of the LDA at $0CE8: the address of the definition sfx_start is copying, written from sfx_defs.

High byte of the definition address in the LDA at $0CE8 (written with $0CE9 by sfx_start from sfx_defs). The loop copies the effect's 20 definition bytes into the channel's slots of sfx_state, then loads the channel number (operand at $0CF4) to set up its voice registers.
Operand of the LDY at $0CF3: the channel number sfx_start was given, saved at $0CD0.
The 30 sound effect definitions, 20 bytes each: attack/decay, sustain/release, frequency limits and steps, pulse values, control bytes, sweep modes, length and switching period.
Sound effect definition 1 (20 bytes, the layout sfx_state names). Played as effect 10, the second sound of a shot thrown (player_fire requests 9 and 10).
Sound effect definition 2 (20 bytes, the layout sfx_state names). Played as effect 6, the charge building while fire is held (player_fire).
Sound effect definition 3 (20 bytes, the layout sfx_state names). Played as effect 16, a creature destroyed (sfx_kill requests 16 and 17).
Sound effect definition 4 (20 bytes, the layout sfx_state names). Played as effect 17, the second sound of a creature destroyed.
Sound effect definition 5 (20 bytes, the layout sfx_state names). Played as effect 11, a pickup (sfx_pickup requests 11 and 27).
Sound effect definition 6 (20 bytes, the layout sfx_state names). Played as effect 27, the second sound of a pickup.

Sound effect definition 7 (20 bytes, the layout sfx_state names). Played as effect 24, the roar of world 1's water, which level 1.1's level_sound requests; it writes this definition's sustain and release ($0DEF) by scroll position, and stage_start sets them to $FF.
Sustain and release of sound effect 7, which stage_start sets to $FF.
Sound effect definition 8 (20 bytes, the layout sfx_state names). Played as effect 7, the flame (player_fire requests 7 and 8 as the flame starts).
Sound effect definition 9 (20 bytes, the layout sfx_state names). Played as effect 8, the flame's second sound.
Sound effect definition 10 (20 bytes, the layout sfx_state names). Played as effect 4, a jump (player_control).

Sound effect definition 11 (20 bytes, the layout sfx_state names). No entry of sfx_effects names it in the file as loaded; entries $13 and $14 (effects 19 and 20) take whatever definition an object's movement script gives (move_objects).
Sound effect definition 12 (20 bytes, the layout sfx_state names). Played as effect 5, the landing thud (sfx_land).
Sound effect definition 13 (20 bytes, the layout sfx_state names). Played as effect 1, the panel face's animation (panel_anim).

Sound effect definition 14 (20 bytes, the layout sfx_state names). Played as effects 14 and 22; 14 is Clyde stepping into water (level 1.1's level_player_water and level 2.1's swim_start request 14 and 15).
Sound effect definition 15 (20 bytes, the layout sfx_state names). Played as effects 15, 23 and 28; 15 is the second sound of stepping into water.
Sound effect definition 16 (20 bytes, the layout sfx_state names). Played as effect 0, the weapons tablet's click (sfx_tablet_click).
Sound effect definition 17 (20 bytes, the layout sfx_state names). Played as effects 2 and 3, the weapons tablet opening (tablet_open).
Sound effect definition 18 (20 bytes, the layout sfx_state names). Played as effect 18 when a hit damages an object (flash_sounds, written into sfx_effects by object_flash_one).
Sound effect definition 19 (20 bytes, the layout sfx_state names). Played as effect 18 when a hit bounces off an unharmed object (flash_sounds).

Sound effect definition 20 (20 bytes, the layout sfx_state names). No entry of sfx_effects names it in the file as loaded; entries $13 and $14 (effects 19 and 20) take whatever definition an object's movement script gives (move_objects).

Sound effect definition 21 (20 bytes, the layout sfx_state names). No entry of sfx_effects names it in the file as loaded; entries $13 and $14 (effects 19 and 20) take whatever definition an object's movement script gives (move_objects).
Sound effect definition 22 (20 bytes, the layout sfx_state names). Played as effect 25.

Sound effect definition 23 (20 bytes, the layout sfx_state names). No entry of sfx_effects names it in the file as loaded; entries $13 and $14 (effects 19 and 20) take whatever definition an object's movement script gives (move_objects).

Sound effect definition 24 (20 bytes, the layout sfx_state names). No entry of sfx_effects names it in the file as loaded; entries $13 and $14 (effects 19 and 20) take whatever definition an object's movement script gives (move_objects).

Sound effect definition 25 (20 bytes, the layout sfx_state names). No entry of sfx_effects names it in the file as loaded; entries $13 and $14 (effects 19 and 20) take whatever definition an object's movement script gives (move_objects).
Sound effect definition 26 (20 bytes, the layout sfx_state names). Played as effect 26.
Sound effect definition 27 (20 bytes, the layout sfx_state names). Played as effects 12 and 13, an extra life collected (player_hit_object).

Sound effect definition 28 (20 bytes, the layout sfx_state names). No entry of sfx_effects names it in the file as loaded; entries $13 and $14 (effects 19 and 20) take whatever definition an object's movement script gives (move_objects).
Sound effect definition 29 (20 bytes, the layout sfx_state names). Played as effect 21, the sound of invulnerability, whose sweep step invulnerable_frame rewrites each time ($0FAA).
Sound effect 29's first sweep step, low byte, rewritten by $CEEB and changed each time by $CF17.
Sound effect 29's first sweep step, high byte, rewritten by $CEEB and counted down by $CF21.
70 bytes between the last sound effect definition and the start-up code at $1000 that nothing in the engine reads: assembler leftovers in the file as loaded.

The engine's first instruction after the game file is loaded. Calls init_hardware ($3656), switches the KERNAL and BASIC ROMs out ($01 = $35), sets the low byte of the KERNAL's NMI vector $0318 to $C1 (so that with the KERNAL in, an NMI ends at the RTI at $FEC1 and RESTORE does nothing), calls $CF2F, clears new_game_flag, sets CIA 1 port A as output and port B as input for the keyboard, and jumps to game_restart.

Starts at most one requested sound effect per call: the first of the three channels whose request flag ($1260-$1262) is set has its flag cleared and the effect definition in $1263-$1265 started by sfx_start. When the in-game music is on, the third channel's check at $1041 is overwritten with RTS (sound_set_music_mode), so effects then use two channels.

Requests sound effect X (0-28). Looks up its channel ($FF86,X), priority ($FFA3,X) and effect definition (sfx_effects, $FFC0,X); if the priority is at least the channel's current one ($125D,Y), it takes the channel: stores the priority, the definition number in $1263,Y and sets the request flag $1260,Y for sfx_play_pending.
Clears the extended colour mode bit (bit 6) of $D011.
Turns all sprites off and sets the extended colour mode bit (bit 6) of $D011; vic_ecm_off clears it again. Called before the screen is redrawn.
Sets bit 6 of $D011 (extended colour mode) and returns; raster_bottom calls it.
Clears the horizontal fine scroll in $D016 and returns. No instruction in the engine refers to it.
Sets $D016 to 40 columns with no horizontal fine scroll, keeping the multicolour bit.

Installs the raster interrupt chain. A is the memory configuration for $01; X and Y are the first raster routine's address, written into the JSR at $1105. Masks both CIAs' interrupts. With carry set the handler is irq_entry_rom_off at $10F2, which saves the registers itself (the KERNAL is banked out), otherwise $10F8, reached through the KERNAL's vector at $0314; it is written to both $0314 and $FFFE. Enables the raster interrupt at line $F9, stops CIA 1 timer A and enables interrupts.
Low byte of the interrupt exit irq_install sets up: $7E for the KERNAL's $EA7E, or $5C for irq_exit at $115C (irq_use_own_exit and irq_use_kernal_exit rewrite it); stored into the JMP at $1111.

High byte of that interrupt exit ($EA or $11). irq_install then enables the raster interrupt ($D01A = $81), acknowledges any pending one, sets raster line $F9 with bit 8 of $D011 clear, stops CIA 1's timer A and enables interrupts.

Raster interrupt handler. Entered at $10F2 (pushes A, X and Y itself) or $10F8 (registers already pushed by the KERNAL). On a raster interrupt it acknowledges it and calls the current raster routine (operand at $1106); the routine returns the next interrupt's raster line in A and the next routine's address in X (low) and Y (high), which are stored for the next interrupt. Leaves through the KERNAL's register restore at $EA7E, or through irq_exit at $115C after irq_use_own_exit.
Low byte of the current raster routine in the JSR at $1105, set by irq_install and by irq_entry from the X each routine returns.

High byte of the current raster routine, from Y. After the JSR, irq_entry stores the A the routine returned as the next raster line ($D012), and both halves of the next routine's address here, then leaves through the JMP at $1111.
Low byte of the JMP at $1111, the interrupt handler's exit ($EA7E or irq_exit), written by irq_install from $10CA.
High byte of the handler's exit, written by irq_install from $10CF.
Sets the border and background colours to black.
Fills colour RAM $D800-$DBE7 with A and both screens, $4400-$47E7 and $4800-$4BE7, with the character code in X (the stores are rewritten with the values each call).
Operand of the LDA at $1125: the colour screen_fill writes into colour RAM, stored at $1120 from the A it was called with. The loop fills $D800-$DBE8 in four strips of 251 bytes.
Operand of the LDA at $1133: the character code screen_fill writes into both screens, $4400-$47E8 and $4800-$4BE8, stored at $111D from X. X counts from $FB down to 1.

Makes irq_install end the interrupt handler with irq_exit ($115C) instead of the KERNAL's $EA7E, by rewriting the two immediate operands at $10CA and $10CF; irq_use_kernal_exit at $1162 puts $EA7E back.
Restores Y, X and A from the stack and returns from the interrupt.
Puts the KERNAL's interrupt exit $EA7E back into irq_install (see irq_use_own_exit).
Disables interrupts and banks the ROMs out, leaving RAM and I/O ($01 = $35).

Raster routine for the bottom of the screen: switches the display to 24 rows while the beam is past the 24-row border line, waits for raster line 0 and switches back to 25 rows, so the VIC never starts the upper and lower borders. Returns no next routine of its own; it is reached through the raster chain's address table.
Reads joystick port 1 ($DC01) into the five flags $1277-$127B, like joy2_read. No instruction in the engine refers to it.
The byte shot_box's BIT $11A9 reads only to skip an LDA hidden in its operand.

Reads joystick port 2 ($DC00) into five flags, one per direction: $127C up, $127D down, $127E left, $127F right, $1280 fire. A flag is zero while its switch is closed (pressed). The masks are written into the AND at $11BE.
Operand of the LDA at $11BC: the byte read from joystick port 2 ($DC00), stored there at $11B2.
Operand of the AND at $11BE: the switch being tested, starting at $10 (fire) and shifted right each pass, so that X = 4 down to 0 gives fire ($1280), right, left, down and up ($127C) their flags.
Selects keyboard rows with A on CIA 1 port A, then reads port B until two reads agree and returns it in A.
Low bytes of the start addresses of the 25 rows of the screen at $4400; screen_row_hi at $11F3 holds the high bytes.
High bytes of the start addresses of the 25 screen rows at $4400 ($44-$47).

Which of the two screens the playfield is being drawn for (0 or 1): stage_start sets 1 after clearing $120C-$126C, and scroll_draw_column flips it with the screen shown ($23BE) each time the column counter wraps; player_find_cell and shot_hits_wall read it to look in the screen on show.
The frame flag: the interrupt (raster_bottom, irq_scroll) adds one each frame, and game_frame, stage_intro_loop and get_ready wait for it and take one off, so the game runs one pass a frame.
Coarse scroll requests: irq_scroll adds one each time the fine scroll wraps, and game_frame and stage_intro_loop take one and run scroll_column.

The screen column scroll_draw_column draws the map's next column into (39 at a stage start), moved on by irq_scroll; player_find_cell and shot_hits_wall add it to a sprite's column to find its character.

Non-zero on frames the objects skip: game_frame and game_frame_music leave out the object updates and collision tests while it is set. game_frame_end and scroll_finish_column write it, and get_ready and raster_ready_icons use it as a counter of their own.
panel_colours' step through its eight colours; get_ready and raster_ready_top use it for the Get Ready screen's colour step.
panel_colours' step through its 15 frames of panel sprite 7; raster_ready_icons uses it on the Get Ready screen.

Set by world 2's levels while Clyde swims (level 2.1's level_player, $A355) and cleared by player_control at $2C5D whenever the level's player routine returns to $2C34, that is when he is not in the level's special state $122B; panel_lower shows sprites 1-3 of the panel only while it is set. (The attract block uses the same byte as the timer between the opening scene's fuzzy poses.)

Clyde is dying: player_hurt adds one. While it is set game_frame leaves out player_control, the fire button and the tablet (only shots_check runs), and game_frame_music runs player_dead in place of the collision tests, does not start the end tune and stops the timer; player_dying_wait clears it.
Set by timer_tick when the time runs out, so that invulnerability cannot save Clyde (player_hurt); get_ready reads it. (The attract block uses the byte for the fuzzy poses' index.)

Set by scroll_column once the scroll passes the level's end ($8B95): Clyde then walks on instead of scrolling, and the level's end objects wake; get_ready uses it as a counter on the Get Ready screen.
Set once the level's end tune has started (game_frame_music), so that it starts once.
Sprite bits that sprites_band1-3 add to the sprite priority register $D01B; death_bubble sets them, player_control clears them.

The first of frame_divider's three flags, which count in binary: $1219 flips every frame, $121A each time $1219 comes back to 0, $121B each time $121A does. panel_anim, player_charge, player_dead, colour_waves and invulnerable_frame pace themselves by them.
The second of frame_divider's counters, read by panel_colours_slow and invulnerable_frame.
The third of frame_divider's counters, read by player_dead to alternate its frames.
stage_intro_loop's alternate-frame flag (flipped each pass; panel_colours runs every other frame); $C943 clears it.
fuzzies_raster's side-on swap: toggled at the end of each phase, so that the high-score page's fuzzies turn round.

Clyde moved this frame: cleared by player_control and counted up by each step; player_animate shows the walk while it is set and the standing frame when it is not. flame_draw and player_fire set it to hold his pose.
Fire is holding Clyde still: player_fire sets it while he throws, and player_control then does not walk him.

Clyde's jump is rising: set when a jump starts and cleared at its top or when he hits a ceiling; player_control and player_animate read it, and while any of $1229-$122B is set the tablet will not open.
Clyde is falling: set when there is no ground under him or a rise ends, cleared when he lands.

The level's special state: while set, the level's own routines run instead of the engine's for fire (level_hook_call), the jump (level_jump_call) and Clyde's frames (level_anim_call); player_control clears it unless the level's player routine skips past $2C5A. player_dead also reads it to choose "GULP!".
A jump requested by pushing up, turned into a rise on the next pass.
The way Clyde faces: 0 right, 1 left; it indexes jump_frames and stand_frames, and flame_draw and player_fire use it for the side of his flame and shots.
Clyde's step in jump_steps: counted down from $17 while rising and up to $1C while falling.
player_animate's countdown of four frames between walking steps.
Clyde's idle count: frames standing still before he turns to face the player; flame_draw also sets it.
Set for shot sprite X when fire is pressed with it free, so that releasing fire throws it (player_fire); cleared when it is thrown and when shots_move removes it.
Set with $1231 when fire is pressed; player_fire clears it when both shots are out.
Shot states: positive for a shot in the air, negative ($80) for the flame, zero for none; player_control will not open the tablet while one is out, and shots_move, flame_end and player_fire keep it.
The fire button's charge, counted up to 36 by player_charge; a full charge breathes the flame; flame_end clears it and shot_hit_object reads it.
Set to $FF with $1235 as the flame starts (player_fire); flame_end clears it.
flame_draw's frame count, 24 frames of breath.
Which shot sprite the next throw uses, X = 0 or 2, swapped after each throw (player_fire).
panel_anim's step count, wrapping at 60 to move $123C on; death_bubble and face_reset clear it.
The panel face's expression stage (0-3), raised by panel_anim every 60 steps and set by panel_anim_stage.
The game is paused: raster_bottom sets it on RUN/STOP and clears it on any joystick movement; game_frame and game_frame_music freeze while it is set.
Fire is held: player_fire sets it while the button is down and clears it on release, when the throw happens.
The number of Clyde's shots in the air (0-2), counted by player_fire and shots_move; 2 also lets player_animate show the walk with fire down.
get_ready_strip's position along the Get Ready screen's creature strip, and the bits raster_ready_strip adds to the sprite enable.
Clyde's x high bit (0 or 1): set as he crosses x 255 to the right and cleared to the left; sprites_player adds it to $D010.
Set by death_bubble so that Clyde's shots and flame stop (shots_check); player_control clears it.
Shot X's read position in its weapon's x path (shot_path), set by player_fire.
Shot X's read position in its weapon's y path.
Shot X has finished its path ($FD in either script): shots_move removes it.
The weapons tablet is up: set to 1 as it starts to open and to $FF when open; player_control hands the joystick to weapons_tablet while it is set, and tablet_close clears it.
Set by weapons_tablet when a weapon is chosen, so that the tablet closes; tablet_close clears it.
The current weapon's shots ignore their path and shot_hits_wall (from weapon_no_path, by weapon_setup).
The tablet is turning left: set by $1ED2 for the six steps of a turn.
The tablet is turning right: set by weapons_tablet for the six steps of a turn.
The halves left in a tablet turn (from 1): each half is six steps of two pixels, so a turn moves the icons the 24 pixels between them.
The steps left in the current half of a tablet turn, 6 down to 0.
While the tablet is up, a countdown of three frames between calls of tablet_icon_colours (game_frame).
The death leap's step, counted by player_dead through jump_steps; player_hurt starts it and kill_attacker sets it.
Clyde is carried by an object (player_carried sets it); the levels' routines read it.
Set by the level's code while Clyde is held in place: player_control then neither walks him left nor stops the scroll for him.
The x high bits of Clyde's shots and flame sprites, a bit each, kept by shots_move and flame_draw and added to $D010 by sprites_player; heart_start (the name entry) uses $1259 for its cursor x.

The hurry-up tune is playing: set by timer_tick when it switches the music on at 15 seconds left. While it is set game_frame_music does not start the end tune and stops the music player while the game is paused. On the high-score page fuzzies_raster counts its phases with it.
The x high bits of Clyde's other sprites, added to $D010 by sprites_player; the name entry's cursor y (heart_start).
player_charge's step through its eight flashing colours.
The priority of the effect playing on each of the three channels (sfx_request compares a new request with it; sfx_update clears it when the effect ends).
The request flags of the three effect channels ($1260-$1262), set by sfx_request and cleared by sfx_play_pending as it starts the effect.
The second channel's request flag.
The third channel's request flag.
The effect definition requested on the first channel ($1263-$1265), looked up in sfx_effects by sfx_request and passed to sfx_start in Y.
The effect requested on the second channel.
The effect requested on the third channel.
The end-of-level delay: object_kill sets 60 when the level's end object dies, and game_frame_end counts it down and finishes the level when it runs out.
Forces Clyde left: when the level's code sets it, player_control moves him as if left were pushed.
Forces Clyde right, as $1268 does left.
Set in the torture chambers: no scrolling, a simpler collision test, Clyde is not stopped when hurt, and the level's routine runs in game_frame_music.
Set to $FF by stage_start with $126E-$1272; stage_main_setup writes it again.
The character column within the current tile (0-3): scroll_column moves the map on a column when it reaches 4.
Clyde's movement this frame: 1 left, 0 right, $FF none (player_control); flame_draw reads it.
The landscape is not scrolling: set while Clyde walks left or stands, cleared when he walks into the right edge; game_frame does not move the spawn distance while it is set.
Cleared by the level's routines (the first world's at $A341) before player_hurt; player_hurt reads it.
The ways the level lets Clyde walk: negative both, zero left only, positive right only ($FF from stage_start; set by the level's code).
The scroll position: the map column at the screen's right edge, counted up by scroll_column; level_begin clears it and the level's events (end tune, objects, end) are placed by it.
The level section Clyde restarts from after losing a life: get_ready and stage_start pick the section's start from it, and level_section_from_scroll sets it from the scroll position.
The read position in the level's band table at $8C03 (level_band_routines).
The read position in the level's colour tables at $8B97 (level_colours_next).
The joystick's up flag, zero while pushed (joy2_read writes $127C-$1280).
The joystick's down flag, zero while pushed.
The joystick's left flag, zero while pushed.
The joystick's right flag, zero while pushed.
The fire button's flag, zero while pressed.
Clyde's x position (low byte; the high bit is $1241).
Clyde's y position.
The screen column of Clyde's character (player_find_cell).
The screen row of Clyde's character (player_find_cell), which picks his height in row_heights.
1 when Clyde's cell is off the map, so that the walls are not tested: player_control sets it each frame and player_find_cell clears it when the cell is valid.
The multicolour bits of Clyde's three sprites for $D01C (7: all three), which sprites_band1-3 add in.
Clyde's sprite frame (sprite 0's pointer), set by player_animate, flame_draw, player_fire and player_dead.
The countdown while Clyde lies dead (player_dead), set to $E6 by stage_main_setup.
The screen column of shot X's character, worked out by shot_hits_wall (wrapping at 40).
Clyde's colour; negative while invulnerability's flashing is off (tablet_open sets $FA); invulnerable_frame and player_charge change it.
The screen row of shot X's cell (shot_hits_wall).
The frame of shot sprite 1 (its pointer), $0F for none.
The frame of shot sprite 2 (its pointer at $47FA and $4BFA), $0F for none.
The x and y of the two shot sprites (sprites 1 and 2), two bytes each from here; shots_move and flame_draw keep them and sprites_player copies them to the VIC.
The y of shot sprite 1 (see $1290).
The x of shot sprite 2 (the second pair of $1290), set by flame_draw and death_bubble beside Clyde.
The y of shot sprite 2; shots_move frees the shot count when both shot sprites' y are zero.
Shot X was fired facing left, so shot_path mirrors its x path.
The colour of shot sprite 1 ($D028), from the weapon's colour (player_fire) or 8 for the flame.
The colour of shot sprite 2 ($D029).
panel_anim's delay before the face animates again.
The x high-bit mask of each shot sprite, used when it crosses x 255.
Shot X has hit something: set by shot_hits_wall and shot_spent, read by shots_move.
Cleared by flame_end with the shots' hit flags.
The current weapon's grade plus one (weapon_setup), which shot_hit_object adds to the damage.
The pseudo-random byte panel_anim steps (times 5 plus $81, exclusive-or $10).
Clyde's invulnerability timer, 127 frames from invulnerable_start.

Clyde's spare hit: stage_start sets it to 1 as each life starts (after every Get Ready screen). While it is set, a touch costs it instead of a life: player_dead skips the death leap and calls player_dying_wait each frame, which after about 40 frames takes it to 0 and starts a spell of invulnerability; the next touch kills (seen live). In water (world 1's water characters, or swimming in world 2) a touch kills whatever. timer_tick clears it when time runs out, and level 3's broom and spikes clear it.

The countdown player_dying_wait runs while Clyde uses up his spare hit ($27, set by stage_start as each life starts, after every Get Ready screen): while it is 38 or more the object that hit him is destroyed, and when it goes below zero the knock ends.

The stage number: 1 is level 1.1, then each level and torture chamber in turn up to 10, the ending; game_new and game_end set it, the ending sets it to $FF so that the game starts again from stage 0, and stage_next ($14B2) adds one. It picks the file to load and the stage's settings.
Set by stage_start; nothing in the engine reads it.
The weapons tablet's opening and closing countdown, set by tablet_close_setup.

The place in owned_weapons of the tablet's right-hand icon, set by tablet_icons_fill and turned by weapons_tablet; the weapon in the middle, the one a choice selects (tablet_close), is the place before it, wrapping to the last owned.
How many weapons Clyde owns.
The colour-cycle position of each of the tablet's three icons (tablet_icon_colour).
timer_tick's frame count, 50 frames to a second.
The object carrying Clyde (player_carried).
Set to 1 when fire is pressed on the Get Ready screen ($3845); get_ready_loop then fades the volume ($12B3) and play starts.
A countdown in the Get Ready loop, reset to $FF at $38AD and counted down by raster_ready_top.
The Get Ready tune's volume, 15 at the start: ORed into $D418 each frame and lowered once the screen is ending.
The music option: set when the in-game music is on; get_ready toggles it, timer_tick switches it on for the hurry-up tune.
The number of sound effect channels by music mode: 3 with effects only, 2 with the music (sound_set_music_mode).
Multicolour 1 ($D022) of each of the six raster bands ($12BD-$12C2), copied from the level's table at $8B97 by level_colours_next. A value with bit 7 set leaves the register as the band above set it.
Band 2's multicolour 1 ($D022).
Band 3's multicolour 1 ($D022).
Band 4's multicolour 1 ($D022).
Band 5's multicolour 1 ($D022).
Band 6's multicolour 1 ($D022).
Multicolour 2 ($D023) of each band ($12C3-$12C8), from the level's table at $8BBB; bit 7 set leaves it unchanged.
Band 2's multicolour 2 ($D023).
Band 3's multicolour 2 ($D023).
Band 4's multicolour 2 ($D023).
Band 5's multicolour 2 ($D023).
Band 6's multicolour 2 ($D023).
The background colour ($D021) of each band ($12C9-$12CE), from the level's table at $8BDF; bit 7 set leaves it unchanged.
Band 2's background colour ($D021).
Band 3's background colour ($D021).
Band 4's background colour ($D021).
Band 5's background colour ($D021).
Band 6's background colour ($D021).

The low bytes of the three band sprite routines ($C0FE, $C061 and $C0B0, with the JSR operands' fixed high byte $C0) that level_band_routines chooses from by the level's band table, whose entries are 0-2.
Four sprite frames, $88 $87 $86 $85, that no engine code reads: level 2.1's level_fire ($A41F) shows them in turn on shot sprite 2, the bubbles Clyde breathes out while he swims.

Tests the 15 objects against a box and calls a handler for each that is inside it. The box is $3B/$3C (the lowest and highest y, against $C260,Y) and $3F/$40 (the x limits, against $C25F,Y), with $44, $45 and $42 saying where it lies against x position 256: each object's ninth x bit is in $C25B, five objects to a byte, read with the byte $3A and the bit $3E. Objects that are dying (state 4 or more), switched off ($023C, $C23D), of type $37 or showing the blank sprite $0F are skipped; an object in state 3 is tested whatever its other flags. A double-height sprite ($C006) gets a second test 15 lines lower. A hit jumps to the handler written at $13CE with the object index in X. In a torture chamber ($126C set) only object 0 is tested.

The branch at $13BE, BNE ($D0) or BEQ ($F0): player_box_x and shot_box return it in Y by the x high bit of Clyde or the shot, and player_collisions and shot_collisions store it here. In the torture chambers ($126C), or when $42 is zero, object_collisions takes this short test: the object is hit when its x high bit (in $41) agrees through this branch and its x lies between $40 and $3F; then it jumps through $13CE to the handler with X = the object.
Low byte of the JMP at $13CD: the handler for an object found inside the box, written with $13CF by player_collisions and shot_collisions.
High byte of the collision handler in the JMP at $13CD.

Starts the death of object X: unless it is already dying (state 4), sets its state, clears $C0FF and $C10E and, for an object showing the blank sprite $0F that is not of type $37, only scores (score_add). Otherwise it gives the object its death type (the low nibble of $C441, through object_set_type) and the death colour cycle named by the high nibble (level tables $8E02, $8E11 and $8E20), scores it, restarts its movement, switches it to its death movements ($C2D9 for x, $C2E8 for y, from the level tables at $8E2F/$8E4F and $8E6F/$8E8F) and makes its sprite multicolour ($C000). Killing the level's end creature (slot $8F0C) within three of the level's end ($8B95) starts the stage-complete countdown $1266 at 60.

Operand of the LDX at $1490: the object object_kill is killing, stored there as it starts. If the scroll position is within three columns of the level's end ($8B95) and that object is the level's end object ($8F0C), it sets the end-of-level delay $1266 to 60.

The number of levels started in this game: 0 until the first game, zeroed by game_new and raised by one by level_begin each time a level starts (1 in level 1.1, 2 in level 1.2, up to 6 in level 3.2, the last torture chamber and the ending). loading_setup gives it to load_route_colour, which paints that many steps of the route on the loading map.
Sets the stage number $12A2 to $FF and falls into stage_next, which takes it to 0: the stage that loads the file 1@ and then the first level.

Starts the next stage: stores X in $14D0, banks the ROMs out, adds one to the stage number $12A2, silences the sound, fills the stack page with $FF, clears zero page from $02 up and jumps to the loading screen at stage_load ($F7CB).

What stage_next was given in X: 1 after the last life and when the ending finishes ($7E72), 0 for anything else (a completed stage, a quit, a new start). It survives the load: loader_hand_over ($BE31, run at $4931 in the copy) adds a life and enters the stage when it is 0, and enters the attract block at $E503, where the high-score check runs, when it is 1.
The page after the file's last, from load_end_pages by loading_setup; fast_loader stops when its page counter $4898 reaches it.
The page the file loads to first, from load_start_pages by loading_setup; fast_loader starts its page counter $4898 from it.

Opens the stage's file on drive 8 through the KERNAL, with the BASIC ROM out and the KERNAL in ($01 = $36). Before the first level (stage 1) it goes straight to the KERNAL calls; otherwise it first prints "LOADING:" (print_at string 12) in the bottom rows and the stage's progress bar from the stage tables at $BF46 and $BF51, with characters built at $5001. Sends the two-character file name ($BF39) with LISTEN and OPEN, then TALK, and reads the first byte. If the drive reports file not found ($90 bit 1 after the read), it asks for the other side of the disk (insert_side_prompt). Otherwise it jumps to the fast loader at $4800.

Operand of the CPX at $1549: the stage's progress-bar marker from load_bar_marker, written at $1513, where the loop that builds the bar's partly filled character at $5001 stops. Then the routine clears the cell after the bar ($47AD plus load_bar_length) and opens the file: SETLFS 1, 8, 0 and SETNAM with the two characters at $BF39, then the KERNAL's LISTEN ($ED0C), SECOND with $F0 (open, $EDB9), the name bytes ($F3F6, which ends with UNLISTEN), TALK ($ED09), TKSA $60 ($EDC7) and ACPTR ($EE13), keeping the first byte in $AE. A drive that does not answer ($90 negative) or a file that is not there ($90 bit 1) goes to insert_side_prompt; otherwise it jumps to the fast loader at $4800.

Prints "INSERT SIDE B AND" and "PRESS FIRE TO START" (print_at strings 13 and 14) in the bottom rows, colours the bottom row, waits for the fire button to be pressed and released, pauses about a third of a second and tries the file again at $14E7.
Set once fire has been pressed in insert_side_prompt, so that a held button is not taken twice.
34 bytes of assembler leftovers before the graphics at $1600; nothing refers to them.
50 NOP instructions and an RTS: a delay. The attract's opening scene calls it twice at $EE93 to time its raster split once the logo is falling.
Three NOPs and an RTS: a delay the attract's line-by-line loop calls at $E8D8.

Resets Clyde's weapons for a new game: the right-hand icon's place $12A5 to 0 and the count owned $12A6 to 1, $CFE2 to 1, owned_weapons to the first weapon alone (frame $57, then the $FF end), all three tablet icons to it, their positions (tablet_icons_place), and the panel's weapon icon (weapon_icon_draw with 0).
Chooses the first weapon (position 0, weapon 0: $1A94 and $1A96 cleared) and sets it up (weapon_setup with X and Y 0). Called at each new game and by add_weapon_fallthrough.

Starts a new game: chooses the first weapon (weapon_select_first), sets the stage number $12A2 to 1, zeroes route_progress, clears the score $B7E4-$B7E7, resets Clyde's weapons (player_reset), sets $CFED to 2, clears the potion counts potions_total-$B8A2, sets the eight bytes $B419-$B420 to $FF and $CFE3-$CFEA to 0 and then makes the first of each 1, and sets the lives $B7BF to 4. Then it runs on into level_begin.

The tail of game_new, also called on its own by the witch's shop ($ECAE) as each later level starts: clears the scroll position $1273 and level section $1274, adds one to route_progress, clears the 20 items-taken bytes from $B96B, resets the stage timer ($ACA6), copies the level's five hook addresses from $8CE8-$8CF1 into the engine's calls at $1CB9, $2C32, $2D76, $2E88 and $1BA6, and jumps to $1D7A.
Stores A, X and Y into $0456, $087C and $0887 (operands inside the music player).

X = 0 for sound effects only, 1 for the in-game music. Sets the number of effect channels (the LDY at $0A68, from $12B5,X: 3 channels or 2) and the opcode at $1041 (from $CEDB,X: LDA or RTS) so that with the music on, effects leave the third voice alone.
Calls music_set_hooks with A = 2, X = $18, Y = $0E.

Starts a level after its file has loaded. Resets the stack, blanks the screen, disables the VIC's interrupts, fills the screen with character $FE, silences the sound and clears zero page $0B-$10 and the object position tables ($C25F-$C27C, $C14A-$C167). Points the IRQ vector at $22E8 and the NMI vector at $22E7, banks the ROMs out, masks the CIA interrupts, calls $CEEB, enables the raster interrupt, calls $3D4A, sets the first interrupt at line $FF, multicolour 40 columns, stops CIA 1 timer A and calls $CF2F. Sets $126D-$1272 to $FF, restores the panel's bytes $2532-$2541 and $2562-$2569 from their copies and enables interrupts. Then clears the variables $120C-$126C, sets up the opening, plays two effects (numbers $15 and $16), and runs the opening loop at $19FB: one pass per frame, until the scroll position $1273 reaches $FF.

The opening's frame loop: waits for the frame flag $120D, then on frames counted by $120E calls $26ED, scrolls $1FC2, updates the eight sprite slots ($1FC6, $1CE1, $1CF3), on alternate frames calls $1D95, counts down the panel timers $2562-$2569 and the bytes $2532-$2541 with the flags in $2519, and updates the sound effects. Leaves when $1273 reaches $FF.

Operand of the LDX at $1A2F: the sprite slot stage_intro_loop's inner loop is on, stored at $1A10 (7 down to 0). After the eight slots, on alternate frames ($121D) it calls panel_colours; then for each of the eight panel sprites it counts down panel_countdowns and, once one is spent, moves that sprite 8 pixels left each frame, flipping its x high bit in $2519 when it crosses 0; then it updates the sound effects.

Operand of the CMP at $1A71: the scroll position at which the opening ends, written by stage_start from the level's table at $8C2F for the level section $1274 (play resumes at the section's start). Below it the loop goes round again (stage_intro_loop).

Sets up play after the opening: selects the music mode from $12B4 (sound_set_music_mode); for stages 1 and 2 (world 1) calls world1_ranges and the level's $A9E2; gives weapon_setup its stage-start weapon; sets Clyde's start position and colour and the sprite multicolours; sets Clyde's sprite pointer (sprite 0, $0F at $47F8 and $4BF8, both screens); on stages 4 to 6 (world 2) writes $32 to $A301 and calls the level's $A302, which sets up the oxygen bar; turns all sprites on ($2A0F), sets the fire branch for play ($1E21) and the dying countdown $1288; and, when the music option $12B4 is on, starts the level's tune (address at $8D56/$8D57) and calls music_hooks_ingame.
Operand of the LDX at $1A93: the weapon position weapon_setup is given at each stage start, kept by weapon_select_first and tablet_close.
Operand of the LDY at $1A95: the weapon number weapon_setup is given at each stage start, kept by weapon_select_first and tablet_close.
Operand of the LDA at $1A9A: Clyde's starting x position ($1281), written by get_ready from the level's data.

Operand of the LDA at $1A9F: Clyde's starting y position ($1282), written by get_ready. Then stage_main_setup sets his colour 10, the sprite multicolours $0B and 7 ($D025/$D026, $1286), blanks sprites 1 and 2 and Clyde's frame (pointer $0F), calls the level's $A302 with $A301 = $32 in world 2 (stages 4-6), enables all eight sprites ($2A0F = $FF), puts BEQ back in the weapons tablet ($1E21), sets $1288 to $E6, and with the music option on ($12B4) starts the level's tune ($8D56/$8D57) with the in-game hooks.

The in-game frame loop, one pass a frame. Waits for the frame flag $120D and takes one off; while the game is paused ($123D) it goes straight to the sound ($1BC2). Otherwise it runs scroll_column for a coarse scroll request ($120E). While the landscape scrolls ($1270 clear) and before the level's end ($1216) it takes the scroll speed off the spawn countdown $1FC2 (unless that is 0 or $FE). It stores the pixels scrolled this frame in $22FB (0 while the landscape stands: the BNE at $1B18 lands inside the BIT at $1B35, on an LDA #0) and, when they are not 0, moves Clyde's two shot sprites left with the landscape and runs objects_scroll. Unless the frame skips the objects ($1210): with the weapons tablet closing ($124C) tablet_close, while it is up ($124A negative) weapons_tablet and every third frame tablet_icon_colours, then shots_check and panel_anim; otherwise invulnerable_frame, and while Clyde is dying ($1214) only shots_check, when shot sprite 1 shows frame $50 or above; else player_control, the level's hook (level_hook_call, while the special state $122B is set) or player_fire, player_animate and panel_anim. Then move_objects, animate_objects and object_colours, unless $1210, and the sound effects (sfx_play_pending, sfx_update), which a dying Clyde's frames skip once $1254 is 0. Continues at game_frame_music.
JSR whose operand ($1BA6) game_new fills from the level's hook table at $8CF0.

Operand of level_hook_call, two bytes written by level_begin from the level's $8CF0: called instead of player_fire while $122B is set. The frame then goes on with player_animate and panel_anim; unless the frame is skipped ($1210), the objects move, animate and are coloured (move_objects, animate_objects, object_colours); the sound effects run unless Clyde is hurt and $1254 is clear.

Second part of the frame. With the music option on ($12B4) it runs music_frame each frame, except while the game is paused with the hurry-up tune's $125A set. It starts the end tune (end_tune_addr, music_play) once, setting $1217, when the scroll position $1273 comes within three columns of the level's length ($8B95), unless Clyde is dying or $125A is set. Then, while Clyde is dying ($1214), player_dead; otherwise, unless paused ($123D, to panel_colours_slow) or skipping objects ($1210, to game_frame_end), player_collisions, then player_dead if that killed him, else shot_collisions for both shots (X = 0 and 2) unless the level's special state $122B is set. Then object_spawn, timer_tick (unless Clyde is dying or $1215 is set), score_draw and potions_draw when their flags say the panel changed, and panel_colours_slow.

End of the frame. Clears the skip flag $1210 and steps the frame-divider bits (frame_divider). While paused ($123D), Q (keyboard row $7F, bit 6) quits through game_end with X = 0. Counts down the stage-complete delay $1266 and on zero goes to the next stage. When the player's energy $1288 is zero, takes a life ($B7BF): with lives left it calls level_section_from_scroll and restarts at the section ($3663); with none it ends the game through game_end with X = 1. Otherwise calls $AC9D and the level's per-frame routine (operand at $1CB9) and loops to game_frame.

Stage-complete countdown: decrements $1266 each frame and, when it reaches zero, starts the next stage (stage_next with X = 0). object_kill sets it to 60 when the level's end creature dies near the end of the scroll.

Takes a life: decrements the lives counter $B7BF. The title's cheat (title_cheat_step in the attract block, CTRL and 2 held on the high-score page once the tune has ended) writes three NOPs over this instruction, and the title puts it back; the C64-Wiki's POKE 7328,208 (unlimited lives) replaces its opcode.
JSR whose operand ($1CB9) game_new fills from the level's hook table at $8CE8: the level's own routine, called every frame.
Operand of level_frame_call, two bytes written by level_begin from the level's $8CE8; after the call the frame loop starts again at game_frame.

Ends the game (X = 1 after the last life) or quits it (X = 0, Q while paused). Silences the SID. On stage 1, with the attract block still at $E000, jumps straight to its $E503 (X = 1) or $E500. From any later stage it sets the stage number to $FF and goes to stage_next with X, which loads the file 1@ and level 1.1 again; loader_hand_over then enters the attract block the same way.
Operand of the LDX at $1CD7: the X that game_end was called with.

Steps the four flags $1219-$121C as the bits of a counter: $1219 changes every call, $121A every second, $121B every fourth and $121C every eighth, so routines can run on every second, fourth or eighth frame.

Moves the 15 objects left with the scrolling. For each object that is dying (state 5) or active ($023C), it counts a sleeping object's wake delay (obj_wake_delay) down, waking it (obj_awake) when the count passes zero; then subtracts the scroll speed ($1DE5, or nothing for objects whose $C39C bit 7 is clear and that move on their own) from the object's horizontal position $C25F (two bytes per object), flipping the object's bit in the position high bits $C25D/$C25C on a borrow.
The horizontal step for this object: Y (the scroll speed) is written into the SBC at $1D55.
Operand of the LDY at $1D4F: the object index, stored at $1D13 so that Y can be reloaded after the step is chosen.
Operand of the SBC at $1D55: the step the object moves left this frame.
Operand of the LDA at $1D5C: the position high-bit byte of the current group of objects ($C25D, then $C25C), decremented after each group of eight.
Operand of the STA at $1D61, kept equal to $1D5D.
Sets the level section $1274 to the first entry of the level's section table ($8C23) that is not below the scroll position $1273: the section the player restarts in after losing a life.
Calls panel_colours on frames where both $1219 and $121A are set (every fourth frame).

Animates the status panel's sprites: steps $1211 through 8 colours (table $1DE7 into the colours of panel sprites 2 and 3 at $254C and $254D, $1DEF into the colour at $25CF set by the lower panel routine) and $1212 through 15 steps (table $1DC7 into panel sprite 7's pointer at $2549, $1DD6 into its colour at $2551).
15 sprite pointers ($B8-$BB) cycled into panel sprite 7 by panel_colours, an animation of the panel icon.
15 colours cycled into panel sprite 7 with panel_cycle_a.
Pixels the landscape scrolls each frame; $1DE6 holds the normal value restored after the weapons tablet.

The scroll speed put back into scroll_speed after a pause ($267F) and when the tablet closes ($1FBF, unless in a torture chamber); saved from scroll_speed when the pause starts ($264C) and when the tablet opens ($2C18).
8 colour values cycled into $254C and $254D by panel_colours.
8 colour values cycled into $25CF by panel_colours.
Sets the tablet's closing countdown $12A4 to 11 frames and the zero-page bytes $53-$56 for it, and clears $24F0.

The weapons tablet, while it is shown ($124A bit 7). Reads the joystick. Fire released (bit set again) selects the weapon in the middle: calls $B44B and tablet_close_setup, sets $124C and closes the tablet through tablet_close. With fire held, left or right starts a turn of the carousel: over six steps the three weapon icons (sprite positions in the panel code at $2572-$257D) slide by two pixels a frame, the one leaving is moved to the other end, the selection $12A5 moves through the list of owned weapons at $2592 ($12A6 of them), and sound effect 0 plays at each step.

Opcode of the branch at $1E21 on the fire flag: BEQ ($F0) in play, set by stage_main_setup at $1AE1, so that fire held reads left and right and fire released selects; the shop block writes BNE ($D0) at $EB4D, so that in the shop the tablet turns with fire released and fire held only sets $CFEE for the shop to act on. The rest of weapons_tablet follows: left (with $127E) steps the selection back (tablet_prev_index) and starts a turn to the right ($124F), right ($127F) steps it on and starts a turn to the left ($124E); each step moves the icons and their sprites two pixels, and partway through each turn the icon that has gone furthest is moved $48 pixels to the other end and given the next owned weapon's pointer, with sfx_tablet_click.
Requests sound effect request 0 (sfx_request with X = 0).
Returns in X the place before $12A5 (the right-hand icon's), wrapping to the last of the $12A6 owned weapons: the middle icon's place.
Clears the three sound effect channels' priorities $125D-$125F.

Counts down $12A4 while the tablet closes ($2B1E each frame), then clears the tablet flags $124A and $124C, sets $24F0 to $FF, frees the effect channels, takes the chosen weapon from the list ($2592 at the selection, minus $57) into $1A94 and its list position into $1A96, restores the scroll speed (unless in a torture chamber) and sets the weapon up through $3102.
Three bytes counted down by the first frame loops ($1A1D, $1B28) by the scroll speed, until they reach 0 or $FE.
Low byte of the address of the next spawn record object_spawn reads: get_ready sets it from the level's section table at $8C6B, and each record read moves it on 17 bytes ($22A0).
High byte of the spawn record address, from the level's table at $8C71 and carried into at $22AA.
RTS: an empty routine.

Spawns the level's objects as the landscape scrolls. $1FC2 counts the scroll distance to the next spawn record; when it reaches zero (or was $FF) the record at $1FC3/$1FC4 is read. Each record is 17 bytes. Byte 0: the object slot (low nibble) and the x movement it takes when it dies (high nibble, $C2D9). Bytes 1 and 2: its x and y movement scripts (bits 0-5, through the level's tables at $8E2F/$8E4F and $8E6F/$8E8F), their top bits together choosing a delay from $8ECF for $C351. Byte 3: its type (bits 0-5), which gives its animation script ($8D5A/$8D92, the first byte its first sprite frame in $C16A) and animation speed ($8DCA), and two flags ($C3BA). Byte 4: its colour, a fixed colour below $10, otherwise a colour cycle (list address from $8E02/$8E11, delay from $8E20). Bytes 5 and 6: its position. Byte 7: what a hit does ($C1D4), which also decides whether its movements and animation run freely or only when it is hit; bit 6 makes its sprite double height ($C006). Byte 8: multicolour (bit 0, $C000) and behind the landscape (bit 1, $C003), scroll flags ($C39C), a linked group (bits 4-6, $C3AB) and bit 7 ($C1E3). Byte 9: hit points ($8EAF, low nibble) and a wake delay ($8EBF, high nibble; obj_wake_delay). Byte 10: score value (low nibble, $C17A) and the y movement it takes when it dies. Byte 11: its death type and death colour cycle ($C441). Bytes 12-14: the x movement, y movement and type a hit can switch it to ($C2F7, $C306, $C315); or, with $FF, byte 13 names a flag in $B96B that stops it spawning once set (an item already taken); or, with $FE, it rides on the object in slot byte 13 at the offsets byte 14 gives ($C450). Byte 15: hits needed to trigger its behaviour ($8EDF) and $C0FF. Byte 16: the distance to the next record. The slot's other tables are cleared, the object is made active, its ninth x bit set ($C25B: objects enter at the right) and the pointer moves on 17 bytes.
Operand of the SBC at $1FE3: 1 when the spawn counter had passed below zero ($FF), else 0.
Operand of the ORA at $2054: the colour-table group from byte 1's top two bits, combined with byte 2's.
Operand of the LDA at $2082 (two bytes, $2083/$2084): the address of the object's movement script, whose first byte is read into $C16A.

High byte of the movement-script address in the LDA at $2082 (written with $2083 by object_spawn). The spawn record's top two bits become obj_flags; record byte 4 picks the object's colour: $10 and up choose colour-cycle list (byte AND $0F) from the level's tables at $8E02, $8E11 (address) and $8E20 (speed), whose first entry is the colour; below $10 the byte is the colour itself.
Operand of the LDA at $20B7 (low byte; $20B9 holds the high byte): the address of the colour-cycle list chosen by record byte 4, whose first entry becomes the object's colour in $C11D.
High byte of the LDA operand at $20B7, written from the level table at $8E11: with $20B8 it points at the colour-cycle list whose first colour the spawned object starts with.
Operand of the LDA at $225D: 0 or 1 from bit 0 of record byte 8, choosing whether the object joins collision group $C000.
Operand of the LDA at $2273: from bit 1 of record byte 8, whether the object joins collision group $C003.
Operand of the LDA at $2289: from bit 6 of record byte 7, whether the object joins collision group $C006.
