Splits an object slot X (0-14) into a group Y (0-2) and a position X (0-4) within it. The objects are drawn in three bands of five on sprites 3-7, so their sprite attribute bytes ($C000, $C003, $C006, $C25B) hold five objects to a byte, at the bits $BF77+X ($08-$80).
Raster routine prologue: saves A, X and Y in $0C-$0E and acknowledges the raster interrupt.
Six NOPs, a short delay, falling into irq_next.
Sets the next raster interrupt: line A, handler X (low) and Y (high) in the vector at $FFFE.
Restores A, X and Y from $0C-$0E and returns from the interrupt.
RTI: the NMI vector points here during play, so RESTORE does nothing.
The first raster routine of a level (stage_start points the vector here, line $FF): chains to raster_top at line 0, waits through the NOP slide, then joins the scroll update at irq_scroll.

Fine scroll, once a frame: subtracts the frame's scroll amount (operand at $22FB) from the fine scroll $10 (0-7); when it passes a character it moves the VSP column $0F on (0-40, then wrapping, with $120F reset to 39) and raises the coarse-scroll request $120E. Raises the frame flag $120D when the scroll amount is 8.
Operand of the SBC at $22FA: the pixels the landscape scrolls this frame (0 while paused).

Raster line 0: chains to raster_vsp_prepare at line $2F, runs $C00D (the sprite multiplexer's first band) and sets the first band's colours: $D023 from $12C3, $D022 from $12BD and $D021 from $12C9, each only when bit 7 is clear.

Raster line $2F: saves A, X and Y into the operands at $23C3-$23C7 and the stack pointer at $23BB, points the next interrupt at raster_vsp on line $30 and enables interrupts inside the handler, then runs the NOP slide so that the next interrupt arrives on a known cycle.

Raster line $30, entered on an exact cycle: points the next interrupt at raster_band2 (line $51), sets the fine scroll in $D016, enters the NOP slide at $1808 plus half the VSP column $0F (one more cycle for an odd column) and then writes $12 and $1B to $D011. The delay decides how many characters late the VIC starts fetching the screen, so the playfield scrolls sideways without characters being copied (VSP). Restores the stack pointer, sets $D018 (operand at $23BE: which of the two screens is shown) and the saved registers, and returns.
Low byte of the JSR at $23AA into nop_slide: raster_vsp writes 8 plus half the VSP column $0F, so the slide is entered further in for a larger scroll.
High byte of that JSR, $18 plus the carry. After the slide the routine writes $12 and then $1B into $D011 with the next raster line ($51) in X for $D012.
Operand of the LDX at $23BA: the stack pointer saved by raster_vsp_prepare, restored with TXS because this interrupt was entered on an exact cycle with the stack left as it was.
Operand of the LDA at $23BD: the value for $D018, choosing the screen at $4400 or $4800 (flipped by $2785) with the character set.
Operand of the LDA at $23C2: the A saved by raster_vsp_prepare, given back before the RTI.
Operand of the LDX at $23C4: the X saved by raster_vsp_prepare.
Operand of the LDY at $23C6: the Y saved by raster_vsp_prepare; the RTI follows.

Raster line $51: chains to raster_band3 at $71, sets the second band's background colours ($12CA, $12BE, $12C4) and calls the band's sprite routine (operand at $23EE, from the level's band table via $26BE).
Operand of the JSR at $23ED: the sprite multiplexer routine for band 2, chosen by level_band_routines.
Raster line $71: chains to raster_band4 at $91, sets the third band's colours ($12CB, $12BF, $12C5) and calls the band's sprite routine (operand at $2418).
Operand of the JSR at $2417: band 3's sprite routine.
Raster line $91: chains to raster_band5 at $B1, sets the fourth band's colours ($12CC, $12C0, $12C6) and calls the band's sprite routine (operand at $2442).
Operand of the JSR at $2441: band 4's sprite routine.
Raster line $B1: chains to raster_band6 at $D1, sets the fifth band's colours ($12CD, $12C1, $12C7) and calls the band's sprite routine (operand at $246C).
Operand of the JSR at $246B: band 5's sprite routine.

Raster line $D1: chains to raster_panel_low at $E3, sets the sixth band's colours ($12CE, $12C2, $12C8), clears the sprite priorities and sets up the status panel's sprites: the weapons tablet's (panel_sprites_tablet) while it is open ($124A), else the score panel's (panel_sprites).

Sets all eight sprites for the weapons tablet: positions from $2572-$2581, pointers from $2582 (both screens' pointer bytes) and colours from $258A; multicolour for sprites 0, 1 and 5-7, no expansion.

Operand of the LDA at $24AB: the sprites panel_sprites_tablet enables in $D015, $FF normally and 0 while the tablet opens (tablet_open, player_control) or after a selection (weapons_tablet). The rest of the routine places the eight sprites from tablet_sprite_xy, sets both screens' pointers from tablet_sprite_ptrs and the colours from tablet_sprite_colours, multicolour for sprites 0, 1 and 5-7 ($E3), no x high bits, expansion or priority, and multicolours $0B and $0F.

Sets all eight sprites for the score panel: positions from $2532-$2541, pointers from $2542 and colours from $254A; multicolour for sprites 6 and 7, sprites 5 and 7 beyond x 255, sprites 0-5 expanded sideways.
Operand of the LDA at $24EF: $FF normally; panel_sprites thus enables all eight sprites. tablet_close_setup clears it, and raster_bottom then takes a shorter delay.

Operand of the LDA at $2518: the score panel sprites' x high bits ($D010), $A0 at a stage start and flipped by the opening's countdowns as the sprites slide in. The rest of panel_sprites sets multicolour for sprites 6 and 7, double width for sprites 0-5, no priority and multicolours $0B and 7.
Score panel sprite positions, x and y for each of the eight sprites; restored from $2552 at each stage start and moved by the opening's countdowns.
Score panel sprite pointers, one per sprite.
Panel sprite 1's pointer (panel_sprite_ptrs + 1), which get_ready writes.
Panel sprite 7's pointer (panel_sprite_ptrs + 7), cycled through panel_cycle_a's frames by panel_colours.
Score panel sprite colours, one per sprite (some animated by panel_colours).
Panel sprite 2's colour, cycled with panel sprite 3's ($254D) from panel_cycle_c by panel_colours.
Panel sprite 3's colour, stepped by panel_colours.
Panel sprite 7's colour (panel_sprite_colours + 7), cycled from panel_cycle_b by panel_colours.
The panel sprites' starting positions, copied to $2532 at each stage start.
Eight countdowns used by the stage opening ($19FB) to slide the panel sprites into place; restored from $256A at each stage start.
Starting values of the eight panel countdowns.
Weapons tablet sprite positions, x and y for eight sprites; the three icon positions at $2576-$257D slide when the tablet turns.
The x of tablet sprite 2, the left icon, moved two pixels a step as the tablet turns.
The x of tablet sprite 3, the middle icon; weapon_icon_show takes the weapon whose icon stands at x $AC.
The x of tablet sprite 4, the right icon.
The x and y of tablet sprites 5, 6 and 7 ($257C, $257E, $2580 for x), moved with the icons as the tablet turns: two pixels a step, and $18 when one wraps round.

Weapons tablet sprite pointers, one for each of its eight sprites (both screens get them, panel_sprites_tablet); $2584-$2586 are the three weapon icons, sprites 2-4, filled by tablet_icons_fill and turned by weapons_tablet.

The pointer of tablet sprite 2, the left icon (tablet_sprite_ptrs + 2): player_reset sets $57, the first weapon; tablet_icons_fill and weapons_tablet change it, and weapon_icon_show and tablet_icon_colours read it.
The pointer of tablet sprite 3, the middle icon, set like $2584's.
The pointer of tablet sprite 4, the right icon (tablet_sprite_ptrs + 4), set by player_reset.
Weapons tablet sprite colours.
The colour of the tablet's left icon, set by tablet_icon_colours from its pointer.
The colour of the tablet's middle icon, set by tablet_icon_colours.
The colour of the tablet's right icon, set by tablet_icon_colours.
The weapons the player owns, as sprite pointers ($57 upwards, one per weapon), ended by $FF; the tablet cycles through them.
owned_weapons from its second entry: player_reset puts the end marker $FF here (one weapon owned), and add_weapon_fallthrough writes the marker through $2593,X after the weapon it adds.
The weapon added at each place in owned_weapons: add_weapon_fallthrough copies $259E,X into owned_weapons at X.
Raster line $E3: chains to raster_bottom at $F1 and, unless the tablet is open, sets the lower panel's sprite colours and multicolour (panel_lower).

Lower panel sprites: multicolour for sprites 2, 3, 6 and 7, colours of sprites 2-4 (sprite 4's from the operand at $25CF); while $1213 is zero, blanks sprites 1-3 (pointer $0F), else waits and sets $D026 from $25F3.
Operand of the LDA at $25CE: sprite 4's colour in the lower panel, animated by panel_colours.
Two values for $D026 chosen by $1213.

Raster line $F1, the bottom of the frame: chains to raster_top at line 0, raises the frame flag $120D (unless the scroll amount is 8), sets extended colour mode for the border area, draws the player's sprites (sprites_player) and saves the objects' positions (objects_save_positions), clears extended colour mode. Then handles the pause: RUN/STOP with the joystick centred pauses (scroll and speed saved, $123D set), any joystick movement resumes. Flips each object's flash colour ($C11D by $C0FF) and finishes with the scroll update.
Operand of the LDA at $2685: the scroll amount saved when the game was paused, restored when it resumes.

Copies the next six band colours of each of the three registers from the level's tables at $8B97 (multicolour 1), $8BBB (multicolour 2) and $8BDF (background), from index $1276, into $12BD-$12CE: a change of sky colours, triggered by a map column command.
Sets the sprite routines of bands 2-5 (the JSR operands at $23EE, $2418, $2442 and $246C) from the level's band table at $8C03 (from index $1275), each entry an index into the routine table at $12CF.

Coarse scroll step, run when the interrupt has requested one. Every fourth step it moves the map on a column ($1273): past the level's end ($8B95) it sets $1216 and wakes objects waiting for the end; a map column with bit 7 set in the level's column command table ($8715) is a command (bit 6: new sky colours, else new band routines) and is skipped. For the six rows of the map (pointers at $8709) it looks up the column's tile and sets the zero-page pointers $C6-$D1 to its character data ($B000/$B060). Each step then draws the tiles' next character column.
Low byte of the LDA at $273E: the map row's column table, from the level's row pointers at $8709 (two bytes per row), written at $2735.

High byte of the map row's table, from $870A. The byte at the scroll position is the tile number, whose character data address (tile_addr_lo/hi) goes into the zero-page pair for the row ($C6,X); six rows, then the column is drawn.

Draws one column of the playfield: for each of the six tile rows, four characters from the tile data, each written into both screens ($4400 and $4800, at the column $120F) with its colour from the level's character colour table at $8609 into colour RAM. When the column counter reaches 39 it first flips the screen shown ($23BE, $120C) and shifts colour RAM left one character, and afterwards copies column 38 into column 38 of the other rows (scroll_finish_column) and sets the skip flag $1210.
When the screens flip, rewrites the last column ($26) of colour RAM from the characters on the shown screen, through the colour table at $8609, for the 24 rows, and sets the frame skip flag $1210.
Stores A through the colour RAM pointer $3E.
Stores A through both screen pointers $39 and $3B, moves the three pointers ($39, $3B, $3E) down one row (40 bytes) and steps the tile data index $40 by four.
High bytes of the two screens, $48 and $44, indexed by the screen flag $120C.
Copies the objects' positions ($C25F-$C27C) to $C14A and their collision group bits ($C25B, without the low two bits) to $C00A, so the next frame's tests see where everything was drawn.

Sets the player's sprites: sprite 0 (Clyde) from $1281/$1282 (position), $1287 (pointer) and $128A (colour); sprites 1 and 2 from $1290-$1293, $128D and $128F, $1295 and $1297; the position high bits from $1241, $1259 and $125B; enables all eight.
Operand of the LDA at $2A0E: the sprites enabled in $D015, $F8 (Clyde and his two shot sprites off) from stage_start for the opening and $FF from stage_main_setup for play.

Animates a status panel sprite at random intervals, on alternate frames. Between animations $1298 holds a delay of 6 or more drawn from the pseudo-random byte $129E (times 5, plus $81, exclusive-or $10); while it counts the last six steps, step X (0-5, kept in the operand at $2A64) copies frame X's graphics, through panel_anim_lo/hi, into the sprite data at $538F. Every 60 steps the counter $123B wraps and $123C goes up (to 3), changing another part of the graphic (panel_anim_stage) with sound effect request 1. $1227 stops it.
Operand of the LDX at $2A63: the animation step, 0-5.
Sets stage X of the panel sprite's second graphic by copying two-byte pieces from panel_stage_gfx into the sprite data at $53A7.
Graphics for panel_anim_stage, two-byte pieces per stage.
The panel face's expression bytes, by stage, that panel_anim_stage copies into the face sprite at $53A8.
Low bytes of the addresses of the six animation frames.
High bytes of the addresses of the six animation frames.
The panel animation's four distinct frames, 14 bytes each (two bytes for each of seven sprite rows); panel_anim_lo/hi play them in the order 4, 3, 2, 1, 2, 3.

Clyde's vertical speed in pixels per frame through a jump, indexed by the jump phase $122E (0-28): small steps near the top of the arc, rising to 8 by the end of a fall. Rising subtracts them, falling adds them.
Added to a screen address's high byte for the screen being drawn: 4 or 0, indexed by the screen flag $120C.

Columns added to Clyde's screen column when his sprite's position high bit is set ($1D, $1D, $1D, $20 by the low bits of his x position). The engine reads only these four; the four after them are a second table that level 1.1's own code reads.

Four offsets from Clyde's screen cell ($8A/$8B) to the characters under his feet: $28, $29 and $2A one row down, $51 two rows down. No engine code reads them; level 1.1's level_player ($A312) tests the characters there for water.

Swaps 64 bytes (one sprite's shape) between the addresses in $53/$54 and $55/$56 and moves both pointers on 64 bytes: one step of exchanging the flame's sprite shapes at $5500 (blocks $54-$5E) with the weapons tablet's at $B100 (tablet_shapes), eleven steps each way.

Counts down $12A4 while the tablet's shapes are swapped in (tablet_swap_step each frame); when done, sets the tablet-open flag $124A to $FF, enables its sprites ($24AC, $24F0), sets Clyde's colour byte $128A to $FA and requests sound effects 2 and 3.

Works out which screen character Clyde stands in: row $1284 from his y position ($1282 minus $32, over 8), column $1283 from his x position less the fine scroll (adding msb_column_offset when his high bit is set) and, unless $126C, the VSP column ($120F), wrapping at 40 onto the next row. Leaves the character's address on the shown screen in $8A/$8B.
Operand of the ADC at $2BB8: the VSP column offset ($120F minus 39) added to Clyde's column.

Clyde's movement, once a frame. Reads the joystick. Down with fire opens the weapons tablet when he is on the ground and nothing blocks it ($1235, $123F, a jump in progress): the scroll stops and tablet_open runs on following frames. Finds his screen cell and calls the level's player routine (operand at $2C32). Up starts a jump ($122C, sound effect request 4). Left and right move him one pixel unless a solid character is in the way: one below the level's first_clear ($8B96), the first character he can pass through; walking right past his limit ($2E5B) starts the landscape scrolling at one pixel a frame instead, until the level's end. Then the jump: rising through jump_steps, falling when there is no solid character below his feet, and landing on the row's height from $2E5E with sound effect request 5. The level's routine at $2D76 is called while $122B is set.
JMP whose operand ($2C32) game_new fills from the level's hook table at $8CEA: the level's routine for the player, run each frame from player_control unless $126C is set.

Operand of level_player_call, two bytes written by level_begin from the level's $8CEA. The level's routine returns to $2C34, or past it. From $2C34: if $122B was set, Clyde's two extra sprites are blanked and his colour set to 7; then $1242, $122B, $1213 and the moved flag $1227 are cleared. Up (with no jump or fall under way) requests a jump ($122C) and sound effect 4. While fire holds Clyde still ($1228) he does not walk. Left (or the level's forced left, $1268), when $1272 allows it, makes him face left ($122D = 1), stops the scrolling ($1270, $22FB) and, unless $1256 holds him or a solid character is to his left, moves him a pixel left down to player_x_min.

Operand of the SBC at $2CD5, 1: the pixels Clyde moves left each frame, written by stage_start. Crossing x 0 clears his x high bit $1241. From $2CF6 right (or the level's forced right, $1269), when $1272 allows it, makes him face right ($122D = 0) and, unless a solid character is to his right, moves him right; at player_x_limit he stops and the landscape scrolls at one pixel a frame ($1270 cleared, scroll_speed 1) until the level's end ($1216).
Operand of the ADC at $2D34: the pixels Clyde moves right each frame, written by player_set_speed.
Operand of the CMP at $2D36: the x position at which Clyde stops and the landscape scrolls instead, from $2E5B.

Operand of the LDX at $2D43: the scroll speed set when Clyde walks into the right edge (scroll_speed), written by player_set_speed. Past the level's end he walks on instead. Not moving at all sets $126F to $FF and, unless $1256 is set, stops the scroll ($1270). Then the jump: while $122B is set the level's routine takes over (level_jump_call).
JMP whose operand ($2D76) game_new fills from the level's hook table at $8CEC, taken while $122B is set.

Operand of level_jump_call, written by level_begin from the level's $8CEC. Otherwise: rising ($1229) goes on at $2DC6, falling ($122A) at $2E24, and a jump request ($122C) starts the rise. With none of these, if there is no solid character under Clyde's feet (three cells, 3 rows down) he starts to fall ($122A = 1, $122E = 0), else he is stood on his row (player_land).
Snaps Clyde to the height of the row he is in ($2E5E by $1284) and, if he moved, requests sound effect 5.

Requests sound effect 5, the landing thud (also used when a rising jump hits a ceiling). From $2DBB a new jump starts: $122C is used up, the step index $122E set to $17 and the rising flag $1229 set. Each frame of the rise takes a step of jump_steps off his y ($122E counting down) unless a solid character is above his head or he reaches line $32; at the top of the rise he falls ($122A), or lands if there is ground under him.
Clyde's rightmost x position before the landscape scrolls, by his position high bit: $C8, or $3B beyond 255.
Clyde's leftmost x position, $1F.
The sprite y position that stands Clyde on each screen row: $35 upwards in steps of 8, 22 rows.
Offsets added to the walking frame base for the eight steps of Clyde's walk: 1, 2, 3, 4, 3, 2, 1, 0.
Clyde's step in walk_cycle (0-7), counted down every fourth frame by player_animate.
Sprite pointer of Clyde's first walking frame for the way he faces, from jump_frames.
Clyde's sprite pointer while jumping or falling, facing right ($49) and left ($44); also the walking frames' base.
Clyde's sprite pointer standing still, facing right ($42) and left ($40).

Chooses Clyde's sprite frame: the level's routine (operand at $2E88) while $122B is set; the jump frame in the air; the standing frame when still, and once the idle count $1230 runs out the front-facing frame $4E, resetting that face's expression to its first stage ($AEE4 with $4C); the walking cycle (walk_cycle, every fourth frame) when moving. Then, unless $1242, moves his shots and flame (the loop at $2F10).
JMP whose operand ($2E88) game_new fills from the level's hook table at $8CEE, taken while $122B is set.

Operand of level_anim_call, written by level_begin from the level's $8CEE. Otherwise in the air Clyde shows his jump frame (jump_frames by facing $122D), with the walk reset; standing still he shows his standing frame until the idle count $1230 runs out, then turns to face the player ($4E, resetting that face to its first expression with face_reset); walking (with fire up, or $123F = 2) he steps through walk_cycle every fourth frame ($122F) from the walking base. The frame goes to $1287.
Unless $1242 is set, falls into shots_move to move Clyde's shots or his flame.

Moves Clyde's two shots (X = 2 and 0, sprites 1 and 2) or his flame. A shot (state $1235 positive) follows its weapon's path (shot_path) unless $124D says otherwise, and is removed when it hits a solid character (shot_hits_wall), finishes its path ($1249), or leaves the screen (above y $33, below $3045, or past the edges); removing one frees its sprite (pointer $0F) and lowers the count $123F. The flame (state negative) is drawn at flame_draw.

Clyde's flame breath: places sprites 1 and 2 beside his head, on the side he faces, with frames from the tables at $AF32/$AF4E (facing left) or $AF02/$AF1A (facing right) for each of its 24 frames ($1238), and holds him in the breathing pose; when the count ends, flame_end.
Sets the position high bits of sprites 1 and 2 for a flame beyond x 255.
Ends the flame: clears both shot states, the charge, the shot count and the hit flags, and blanks sprites 1 and 2.
The lowest y a shot may reach ($BF) before it is removed.

Moves shot X one step along its weapon's two path scripts, one for x (through the operand at $305B) and one for y ($30BC), with read positions $1245,X and $1246,X. A byte of 0 holds still for the frame, $FD marks the path finished ($1249,X), $FE repeats the step before, $FF restarts the script from its second byte; otherwise bit 7 means backwards and the low seven bits are the pixels to move. For a shot fired facing left the x direction is mirrored by turning the BPL at $3081 into a BMI.
Operand of the LDA at $305A (two bytes): the address of the current weapon's x path script, set by weapon_setup.

High byte of the LDA operand at $305A, the x path script's address, from weapon_xpath_hi by weapon_setup. The code after it acts on the x byte as shot_path says; on $FF it sets the read position to 1, and since A is then 1 the BEQ at $307F is not taken, so the restart frame moves the shot one pixel instead of reading the script.
Opcode of the branch at $3081, rewritten by shot_path: BPL ($10) for a shot fired right, BMI ($30) for one fired left.
Operand of the SBC at $308C: the step of a backward x move.
Operand of the ADC at $30A8: the step of a forward x move.
Operand of the LDA at $30BB (two bytes): the address of the current weapon's y path script, set by weapon_setup.

High byte of the LDA operand at $30BB, the y path script's address, from weapon_ypath_hi by weapon_setup. The code after it reads the y byte like the x byte: 0 holds, $FD finishes the path, $FE repeats the step before, $FF reads position 1 at once; bit 7 moves the shot up by the low seven bits, otherwise down.
Operand of the SBC at $30EC: the step of an upward move.
Operand of the ADC at $30FC: the step of a downward move.

Sets up weapon X at grade Y: the addresses of its x and y path scripts ($B574/$B57C and $B584/$B58C into shot_path's operands), whether its shots ignore the path ($B411 into $124D), and its shot colour from the grade (through $B419 and the colour table at $CED6 into $CED5), with the grade plus one in $129D.
Finds the screen character under shot X (as player_find_cell does for Clyde) and sets $129A,X when it is solid (below the level's first_clear, $8B96).
Operand of the ADC at $3189: the VSP column offset added to the shot's column.

The fire button. While fire is held Clyde takes his throwing pose and, if a shot sprite is free (fewer than two shots, $123F), a charge starts ($1231, $1236 counting up to 36 frames, sound effect request 6); a full charge flashes his colour (player_charge). When fire is released: after a full charge with no shots in the air, he breathes the flame (24 frames, both shot sprites, sound effect requests 7 and 8); otherwise a shot leaves from beside him in the direction he faces, with the sprite from $3306/$3308 and the weapon's colour $CED5, and sound effect requests 9 and 10.
Counts the fire button's charge $1236 up to 36; while it is full (and $129F and $128A allow), Clyde's colour cycles through the eight colours at $32FE every other frame ($125C).
The eight colours Clyde flashes through while a flame is charged.
Sprite pointers of a shot: $81 and $83 fired right (low and high), $82 and $84 fired left.
The shot sprites of the weapons (with $3306), read by player_fire.
memory_swap's table of page counts minus one, for swaps 0-10; swap_from ($3315) and swap_to ($3320) follow.
High bytes of the first block of each memory_swap: $F2, $D8, $E0, $A0, $50, $50, $58, $58, $9A, $E0, $16.
High bytes of the second block of each memory_swap: $40, $58, $7B, $60, $58, $D0, $D0, $E0, $E0, $60, $60.

Exchanges two blocks of memory, whole pages, with all RAM visible ($01 = $24): swap X (0-10) takes its page count, first and second block from swap_pages, swap_from and swap_to. 0 exchanges the drive code page at $4000 with $F200; 1 $D800 with $5800 (8 pages); 4 $5000 with $5800; 5 $5000 with $D000; 6 $5800 with $D000; 7 $5800 with $E000 (18 pages, the file 1@ into the engine's code block); 8 $9A00 with $E000 (18 pages, the second level's replacement block); 2, 3, 9 and 10 the others in the tables. Ends with RAM and I/O banked in ($01 = $35).
Operand of the LDA at $3347: the first block's page, from swap_from.
Operand of the LDA at $334B: the second block's page, from swap_to.
Operand of the LDX at $334F: the number of pages minus one, from swap_pages.

Prints text string Y on the screen at the address A (high) X (low), the string's address taken from print_at_lo/hi ($33B9/$33CF). Converts the text's ASCII as it goes: space becomes character $FF; digits, '-', '.', ',' and the apostrophe are kept; letters lose $40 (so 'A' is screen code 1). Stops at a byte with bit 7 set.
Low byte of the LDA operand at $337E, the string's address, from print_at_lo.
Operand of the LDA at $337E (two bytes, $337F/$3380): the address of the string being printed.
Operand of the STA at $33B2 (two bytes, $33B3/$33B4): the screen address being printed to.
High byte of the STA operand at $33B2, the screen address, written at $336A from A; the low byte at $33B3 is X, and the STA adds the position in the string.

Low bytes of the addresses of print_at's 22 strings: 1 "COLLECT THE FOLLOWING CREATURES", 2 "FOR MAGIC POTIONS", 12 "LOADING:", 13 "INSERT SIDE B AND", 14 "PRESS FIRE TO START", 15-21 the title's lines ("CLYDE RADCLIFFE EXTERMINATES ALL" to "COPYRIGHT THALAMUS 1990"); 0 and 3 point into the level's data at $8C87 and $8CB0, and 4-11 are zeros, of which the ending points 4-7 at its story and its cheat hint.
High bytes of the addresses of print_at's strings.

Prints string Y in the big two-by-two letters at the screen address A (high) X (low), the string's address from print_big_lo/hi. Each letter is four characters from big_font (top left, top right, bottom left, bottom right), one or two columns wide: space advances one column, '.' and ',' have their own shapes, digits are shifted to theirs, I is narrow and M and W take an extra column (character $28 or $29). Ends at $FF.
Operand of the LDA at $3401 (two bytes): the address of the big string being printed.

High byte of the LDA operand at $3401, the big string's address, from print_big_hi. The code after it, to $347A, gives each character a shape and a width (as print_big says) and draws the shape with big_put four times: the top row at Y = 0 and 1, the bottom row at $28 and $29.
Operand of the ADC at $347F: how many columns the screen address moves on after a big letter (1 or 2), written at $3411 and $3456.
Operand of the LDA at $3489: an extra column for the wide letters M ($01) and W ($FF), zero otherwise.
Operand of the LDY at $3497: the position in the big string.
Stores A at the screen address in the operand at $349F plus Y, and moves Y on.
Operand of the STA at $349E (two bytes, $349F/$34A0): the screen address of the current big letter, moved on two columns per letter.
High byte of the STA operand at $349E, the big letter's screen address, written by print_big from A and carried into when the low byte at $349F passes a page ($3486).

Low bytes of the addresses of print_big's 19 strings: 0 "GET  READY", 4 "TODAYS TOP HEROS", 15 "LOADING   . ", 16 "GAME OVER", 17 "YOU'RE IN THE TOP 8", 18 "....", others in the level's data ($8C7D, $ABF3, $ABF5) or the high-score area ($C9E0, $C9E8); 5-12 are zeros, and the ending points 5 and 6 at its "GAME COMPLETE" and "THE END".
High bytes of the addresses of print_big's strings.
"GET  READY", the big text of the Get Ready screen, ended by $FF.
"COLLECT THE FOLLOWING CREATURES" and, at $34F4, "FOR MAGIC POTIONS": the Get Ready screen's two lines, each ended by $FF.
The big letters' shapes: four character codes per letter (top left, top right, bottom left, bottom right), from A, used by print_big.
big_font from its second byte: print_big reads each shape's top-right character at $3507,X.
big_font from its third byte: print_big reads each shape's bottom-left character at $3508,X.
big_font from its fourth byte: print_big reads each shape's bottom-right character at $3509,X. These 64 bytes are shapes 0-15's last bytes.
big_font from shape 16 (Q) to its last, shape 43: the rest of the letters and the further shapes print_big chooses for other characters.
Colour ramps (black through the greys and colours and back) used by the screens' raster colour bars; colour_bar_delays ($35D6) and colour_bar_colours ($35E6) are read by colour_bars.
Background colours colour_bar16 writes into $D021, line by line.
Delay counts, one per line of the Get Ready screen's colour bar.
The line counts for the Get Ready screen's colour bars, read by four of its raster routines.
The 16 background colours of the Get Ready screen's colour bar.
Background colours of the Get Ready screen's upper bars and creature row.
Background colours of the Get Ready screen's lower bars.
Background colours of the Get Ready screen's icon row.
Raster routine: changes the background colour sixteen times down the screen (colour_bar_colours), waiting the counts in colour_bar_delays between them; returns line $4A and the next routine $3925.
Sets the music player for a full tune: all three voices (A = 0), all registers but the volume copied ($17 down to 0).
Sets the music player for a full tune: all three voices, all 25 registers copied ($18 down to 0).

Prints "GET  READY" in big letters at $4523.

The Get Ready screen, before each level and after each lost life. Blanks the screen, resets the scroll, the panel ($B7C0, $B840, $B8D1) and the sprites, fills six rows from $45B8 with the level's backdrop character ($8D55), swaps the Get Ready characters in (memory_swap 6, $CF82, swap 3), prints "GET  READY" and the stage's name (print_big string 1 from the level's data), the level's lines (print_at strings 0 and 3) and "COLLECT THE FOLLOWING CREATURES" / "FOR MAGIC POTIONS", and draws the music icon. Then sets the level section $1274 up from the level's section tables: the scroll position ($8C29), the Get Ready strip ($8C35, $8C3B), the strip marker's position ($8C41, $8C47), sky colours and band routines ($8C4D, $8C59, $8C53), Clyde's start ($8C5F, $8C65 into $1A9B and $1AA0) and the spawn list ($8C6B, $8C71, $8C77). Turns the music option off, starts the Get Ready tune (at $B97F, all voices) with the volume at 15, and installs the screen's raster chain ($389B).

The Get Ready screen's frame loop: plays the tune with the volume $12B3 (fading), and waits for fire. Fire starts the fade-out ($12B1); a long wait without fire ($1211 reaching 50) also fades. When the volume reaches zero the screen is blanked, the Get Ready characters are swapped out again (memory_swap 3 and 6), the sound is silenced, the music option chosen ($12B4) is kept in the operand at $37A7 and the level starts at stage_start.

Counts the half-second flash of the screen ($C8, $1211), scrolls the strip (get_ready_strip) and chains to $3925 (or $3612).

Operand of the LDA at $395D: the strip marker's y position, from the level's table at $8C47.

Scrolls the Get Ready screen's landscape strip two pixels a frame until it has run its course ($C6 reaching $FF, then $1216 is set). At each whole character it shifts the strip's six rows ($45B8-$46A7 and their colour RAM) left and draws the next column at the right from the level's six map rows ($8715, $87D5, $8895, $8955, $8A15, $8AD5 at column $3BB1), each map byte used directly as a character with its colour from the level's table at $8CF5: a miniature of the level, one character per tile. The map column the Get Ready strip draws next.

Rotates byte list X by one place, left with carry set and right with it clear. Each list's address and length come from the tables at $BEF8, $BF05 and $BF12; used to cycle colours and the creatures' shapes.

Sets the horizontal bounds of a box around Clyde for the collision tests: $3F = x + 16 and $40 = x - 15, with their high bits in $3D and $3E. Returns Y = $D0, or $F0 when his position high bit is set.
Sets the vertical bounds of the box around Clyde: $3B = y + 15 and $3C = y - 15.

Tests Clyde against the objects: points object_collisions' handler ($13CE/$13CF) at player_hit_object, takes the box around Clyde from player_box_x ($13BE, $44) and player_box_y, and jumps to object_collisions. Called each frame from game_frame.
Writes 5 into the flag in $B96B named by the touched object's spawn record ($C21F, from record byte 13), so that object_spawn does not spawn it again.
Requests sound effects 11 and 27, the sound of a pickup.

Handler for an object touching Clyde (X = its slot). The engine tells objects apart by the sprite frame they show ($C16A). Frames $B6-$BB are the Magic Potion Creatures: the touched one adds 1 (5 if its sprite is double height, $C006) to the counter of its kind ($B8A0-$B8A2, through $CECF) and to the total at $B89F, is removed, and is marked taken. Frame $4E (Clyde's face) is an extra life: lives ($B7BF) plus one, a fresh spell of invulnerability ($CEEB), the panel's lives digit redrawn ($B7C0). Other frames are checked against the stage ($12A2): in world 1 frames $88-$8A and $CD carry Clyde (player_carried) and frames $E5-$E9 are harmless; in world 2 frames $85-$88 call the level's routine at $A302; in world 3 the five frames listed at $A300 are harmless and frame $8F calls the level's routine at $A305. Anything else hurts Clyde (player_hurt).
Operand of the LDY at $3C83, written at $3C6D with the Magic Potion Creature's frame minus $B6 (0-5), which picks its counter from potion_counters.

Clyde touched something deadly. Nothing happens while the invulnerability timer $129F runs, unless the hit is the time-out ($1215 set) or water ($1271 clear by the level's player routine), or while the weapons tablet is closing ($24F0 = 0). Otherwise it counts the death in $1214 and $1254, stops Clyde and the scroll ($1270, $22FB, $1DE5) when not in a torture chamber ($126C), starts the dying animation ($AEEF) and, unless Clyde still has his spare hit ($12A0 = 1, when player_dying_wait does it instead) or the hit was the time-out ($AC7E negative), destroys the object that hit him ($AC7D).
World 2's check (stages 4 and 5): sprite frames $85-$88 hand over to the level's own routine at $A302; anything else hurts Clyde.
World 1's check (stages 1 to 3): frame $CD and the eight frames in carrier_frames are not deadly; of those, frames below $E5 carry Clyde unless he is already carried ($1255); anything else hurts him.
Sets Clyde's walking step (the ADC operand $2D35) and the scroll speed written at $2D44 to X: 1 normally (game_new), 2 while he is carried.
The eight sprite frames player_hit_world1 treats as not deadly: $88, $89 and $8A (objects that carry Clyde) and $E5-$E9 (which do nothing to him).

Clyde is caught up by object X: records it in $12B0, clears its $C360 and $1259, sets the carried flag $1255, doubles Clyde's and the scroll's speed (player_set_speed with 2), sets $1295 to 12 and resets the front-facing face's expression ($AEE4 with $4C).

Tables read by the levels' own code while Clyde is carried (in level 1.1, level_anim at $A494-$A4F5), indexed by his facing ($122D): $3D77 his sprite frame ($86, $87) for $1287, $3D79 the raft's frame ($8A, $88), $3D7B the oar's frame ($8B, $8C) for shot sprite 1 ($128D). Then, by paddle stroke ($1258, 0-3), the addresses of the oar's nine-row shapes copied into those blocks: $3D7D/$3D81 facing right, $3D85/$3D89 facing left. The first left-facing shape is in the engine itself, at $3D8D.
The first left-facing oar shape (nine bytes, one sprite column), reached through $3D85/$3D89 rather than by name; the other seven shapes are in the level ($6140-$617E).
Four bytes ($00 $00 $01 $01) after the oar shape that no code found in the engine or level 1.1 reads.

Sets up the box tested around one of Clyde's shots (X): for a shot type ($128D) below $81 a box of 18 by 20 lines (at $3DCE/$3DDA and $3E24/$3E25), otherwise 9 or 10 wide and 4 or 17 high depending on the type. The horizontal limits come from the shot's x position $1290,X; returns Y=$D0 or, for a shot still moving ($1259,X), $F0, as the mask of objects to test.
Operand of the ADC at $3DCD: half the shot box's width to the right, set by shot_box (18 for small shots, 9 for others).
Operand of the SBC at $3DD9: half the shot box's width to the left, set by shot_box (18 for small shots, 10 for others).
Sets the shot box's vertical limits $3B and $3C from the shot's y position $1291,X plus $3E24 and minus $3E25.

Tests one of Clyde's shots (X) against the objects: points object_collisions' handler at shot_hit_object, builds the box (shot_box, shot_box_y) and runs object_collisions. A shot of type $0F (none) is skipped. Called twice a frame from game_frame, once for each shot.
Lines below the shot's y position that the shot box reaches, set by shot_box (20, 4 or 17).
Lines above the shot's y position that the shot box reaches, set by shot_box (38 for small shots, 21 for others).
Kills object X and, if it belongs to a linked group ($C3AB), every other active object of that group whose $C3AB matches (the comparisons at $3E36 and $3E44 are rewritten with X and the group).
Operand of the CPX at $3E36, written at $3E31 with the slot first killed, so the loop does not kill it twice.
Operand of the CMP at $3E44, written at $3E2E with the linked group number of the object killed first.
Requests sound effects 16 and 17, the sound of a creature destroyed.

Handler for a shot touching object X. Objects showing the blank sprite $0F, dying (state 3 or more) or switched off are ignored, as is sprite frame $8E from stage 7 on. Records the hit ($CEC2), then: hit points ($C1F2) of $FF make the object unharmed, flashing only. Otherwise the damage is $129D (the weapon's strength), or 1 when the fire button had been charged for 36 frames or more ($1236); hit points falling below zero kill it and its linked group (object_kill_linked, sfx_kill). A survivor counts the damage in $C201 towards its threshold $C210 (unless $C201 is $FF); reaching it resets the count from $C1E3 and runs the behaviour in $C1D4: bits 0-1 = 1 jump to $CEB2, 2 run one of four special responses ($2A, $06, $12, $16), 3 jump to $BEE6; otherwise bits 2-3 ($AE42, $CEA4) and bits 4-5 ($CE60, $CE80) choose. An object still able to flash (bit 7 of $C12C) then flashes white (object_flash).
Operand of the SBC at $3E9B, written at $3E96: the damage the hit does, 1 for a charged shot or the weapon's strength $129D.
The sound-effect definitions written into sfx_request's table at $FFD2 by object_flash_one: $12 for a hit that damages, $13 for one that bounces off an unharmed object.
Flashes object X after a hit (Y=0 damaged, 1 unharmed), unless it is already flashing ($C12C positive); an object in a linked group flashes with every active object of the group.
Operand of the CMP at $3F5D, written at $3F4E with the linked group whose objects flash together.

Starts object X's hit flash: saves its colour ($C11D into $C12C) and $C0FF (into $C10E) for object_updates to restore after three frames ($C13B = 2), turns it white unless it was unharmed (Y=1), clears $C0FF, and plays sound effect 18 with the definition from flash_sounds.
Operand of the LDY at $3F6C, written at $3F46 with object_flash's Y: 0 for a damaging hit (the object turns white), 1 for an unharmed one.

For each stage of the loading screen's map, how many entries of load_route_hi/load_route_lo load_route_colour paints: 0, 8, 12, 17, 25, 31 and 36.
High bytes of the colour RAM cells ($D9xx/$DAxx) that mark the route already travelled on the loading screen's map, 36 of them, ended by zero.
Low bytes of the same colour RAM cells, paired with load_route_hi.

Runs each frame while Clyde, touched with his spare hit in hand ($12A0, player_dead), is knocked: counts down $12A1. While it is 38 or more the object that hit him keeps being destroyed ($AC7D); when it goes below zero, his dying flags $1214 and $1254 are cleared, the spare hit $12A0 is used up and a spell of invulnerability started ($CEEB).

Destroys the object that hit Clyde, whose slot player_hit_object wrote into this LDX: with its linked group (object_kill_linked) unless $C450 is set and $C3BA clear, and plays the kill sound (sfx_kill) either way.
Operand of the LDX at $AC7D: the slot of the object that last touched Clyde, written by player_hit_object; the time-out writes $FF here.

Writes $7F to both CIA 1 ports. On port A that drives keyboard row 7 alone (1, the left arrow, CTRL, 2, SPACE, C=, Q and RUN/STOP), so port B then reads those keys along with joystick 1, which title_cheat_step in the attract block relies on; port B is an input, and the write there changes nothing that is read.
Copies the level's time limit, three digits at $8CE5-$8CE7, into the timer $B718-$B71A and draws it (timer_draw). Called at each new game and from get_ready.
The y position below which a dying Clyde has fallen out of sight, by $126C: $B8 on a level, $CD in a torture chamber.

Runs each frame while Clyde is dying ($1214). While $1254 counts up the death leap (jump_steps, 29 steps) he rises and falls; once it stops he lies still while $1288 counts down, flickering between his front-facing frames $4E and $4F below 25, and fire skips the wait once it is under 125. When the leap ends on solid ground, or he falls below death_floor, the leap finishes: a speech bubble is drawn into sprites $50/$51 (death_bubble), "GULP!" when he has fallen into the water characters listed at $A300 (world 1) or with $122B set (world 2), otherwise "EEEK!" or "OUCH!" by the frame counter $1219, the death tune plays and his shots are replaced by the bubble's two sprites. With his spare hit $12A0 still set there is no leap: unless he is in water, each frame goes from $AD24 to player_dying_wait, and the touch costs the spare hit instead of a life.
Operand of the CMP at $ACFC, written at $ACF5 from death_floor: the y position at which the dying Clyde has left the screen.

Draws Clyde's exclamation into the speech-bubble sprite $50 (21 bytes at $540C, seven rows of 24 pixels) from one of the three patterns at $BFC8, $BFDD and $BFB3 (X = 0, 1 or 2), places the bubble's two sprites ($50 and $51, as shot types $128D/$128F) beside him, resets the panel animation and some of Clyde's state, silences the effects, and starts the death tune (music_play with death_tune, $BC2B) at full volume (music_hooks_all_vol).
Low byte of the LDA operand at $AD79, written at $AD6E from bubble_text_lo: where the exclamation's 21 bytes are read from.
High byte of the LDA operand at $AD79, written at $AD74 from bubble_text_hi.
Clyde's two front-facing frames ($4E, $4F) that player_dead alternates by the frame counter while he lies dead.
Low bytes of the three exclamations' bitmaps: EEEK! ($BFC8), OUCH! ($BFDD), GULP! ($BFB3).
High bytes of the three exclamations' bitmaps, paired with bubble_text_lo.

Four groups of eight bytes from which the fast loader builds its decoding tables at $4B00-$4B1F: for each of the eight possible readings of the serial port, the two received bits shifted into each of four positions ($A0/$50/$0A/$05, $20/$10/$02/$01, $80/$40/$08/$04 and zero).
Opens the disk drive's command channel (LISTEN to device $BA, secondary address 15) and sends "M-", the start of a memory command.

Shot response 4 (behaviour bits 2-3 = 1): switches the object to the x movement script its record named ($C2F7, record byte 12, through the level's tables at $8E2F/$8E4F), once; then the remaining bits are handled at $3F20.

Returns in A the colour for character A, from the loading screen's table: the character is looked up in the list at $FA53 and the colour taken from the same position at $FA88. Called while the loading screen is copied ($F8CF).
Operand of the LDA at $AE67, written at $AE60 with the character whose colour is wanted.
Operand of the LDA at $AE7D, written at $AE76 with the colour found, which the routine returns.

The tune that starts when the stage timer reaches 15 (music_play at $B772). Header: voice 2 starts $0009 and voice 3 $0012 bytes after $AE84; the data runs to $AEE4, a command's unused second byte that is also face_reset's first.

Resets the front-facing face (sprite $4E, which is both Clyde turned to the player and the panel's lives icon): writes A over the opcode at $AEEC, clears the step count $123B and runs panel_anim_stage with stage 0. Twenty flags, one for each item a level can hold only once (named by a spawn record's byte 13); item_taken sets one, object_spawn skips the item while it is set, and a new game clears them.

The Get Ready screen's tune (music_play at $37EF). Header: voice 2 starts $006B and voice 3 $0188 bytes after $B983, where voice 1 starts; with its sections the data runs to $BC2B, a command's unused second byte that is also the first of death_tune.

The tune for a lost life (music_play at $AE03). Header: voice 2 starts $0051 and voice 3 $0084 bytes after $BC2F; the data runs to $BD00, a command's unused second byte that is also fast_loader's first.

The fast loader, copied with the rest of $BD00-$C0FF to $4800-$4BFF (copy_loader at $F907) and run there. It uploads 256 bytes of drive code from $4000 (where memory_swap 0 has placed it, from $F200) in eight "M-W" commands to the drive's $0700-$07FF and starts it with "M-E" at $07AB. It then builds the decoding tables at $4B00 (loader_nibbles), and receives bytes through $DD00 two bits at a time (load_byte), storing them from page $14D2 up to page $14D1. Every few blocks it advances the loading screen's progress bar (row $47AC) and the marker sprite at $5000 (tables $BF72-$BF83). It ends in loader_hand_over.

The receiving STA, whose operand $BD97/$BD98 (at $4897/$4898 in the copy that runs) is the load pointer: the low byte is incremented after each byte, and the high byte, set from $14D2, after each page until it reaches $14D1.
The LDX's operand; the $E000 block's BIT $BDEC at $EE4F is a skip idiom, not a reference to this byte.

Runs once the stage's file is in. Stage 0 (the file 1@) swaps it to $E000 (memory_swap 7) and goes on to load stage 1 ($14B2). Stage 2 swaps the shop block, which arrived at $9A00, with level 1.1's bytes that loading_screen parked at $E000 (memory_swap 8). Then it sets CIA 1's port directions, the sound mode, releases the keyboard, waits for raster line 0, blanks the screen, sets multicolour text and the black border, and swaps the drive code out and the sprites in (memory_swaps 5 and 0). With end_flag 0 the lives go up by one and the stage starts: a torture chamber (part digit "3") at $8051 after setting $CFED and the objects' $C24C to 2 and the panel's weapon icon, the ending (stage 10) at $7D6A, a level at $E500. With end_flag 1 (the reload after the last life, or after the ending) it enters at $E503.
The second page that copy_loader copies with LDA $BE00,X; here the address falls on the high byte of the JMP $14B2, not on anything of its own.

Receives one byte from the drive (run at $4965 in the copy): signals ready through $DD00, waits for the drive, avoids bad lines (raster above $31 with the low bits 2), then reads $DD00 four times, each reading's two data bits looked up in the four decoding tables at $4B00, $4B08, $4B10 and $4B18 and ORed together.

Gives object X the type Y: sets $BECF and its animation script ($8D5A/$8D92 into $C29D/$C2AC) and speed ($8DCA into $C3D8), restarts the script ($021E = $FF, $C3C9, $C3E7) and sets it running ($C360 = 1).
The type of each of the 15 objects (record byte 3, bits 0-5), which selects its movement script; type $37 marks an object the collision tests skip.
Shot response $2A: pauses the object's animation for two steps ($C324), then carries on with the remaining behaviour bits at $3F0C.
Shot response 3, for an object that animates only when hit: sets $C360 to $FF so that animate_objects runs its script again, then carries on at $3F0C.

rotate_bytes' table of thirteen byte lists: for list X, the low byte of its address here, the high byte at $BF05 and the length at $BF12. 0 and 1 colour_ramps ($35B6, $35C6, 16 each), 2 ready_bar_colours (18), 3 $CA1E (15), 4 title_row_colour (16), 5 title_bottom_colours (16), 6 heart_colours (40), 7 and 8 the attract's $E5CA and $E5DE (20 each), 9 to 12 the attract's $EA6C, $EA9C, $EACC and $EAFC (48 each).
The third page that copy_loader copies with LDA $BF00,X to $4A00; it falls inside strip_tables.
Second part of strip_tables, read by rotate_bytes with LDA $BF05,X.
Third part of strip_tables, read by rotate_bytes with LDY $BF12,X.
Colours for the Get Ready screen's colour bars (raster_ready_top at $38F0).
Sprite pointers for the Get Ready screen, copied at $37B2.

The progress bar's current length on the loading screen, set from load_bar_length and counted down by the loader.
The progress marker's position, set from load_bar_marker and advanced by the loader.
The eight single bits, $01 to $80, used to build sprite and multiplexer bit masks; $BF77 is the same table from $08, for sprites 3-7.

The exclamation OUCH!, seven rows of three bytes.

Background-priority bits for the second band of objects.
Background-priority bits for the third band of objects.
Double-height bits ($D017) of the objects' sprites, one byte per band; object_collisions tests a tall object twice.
Double-height bits for the second band of objects.
Double-height bits for the third band of objects.
Ninth x bits ($D010) of the objects' sprites for each band, made from $C25B by objects_save_positions.
Ninth x bits for the second band of objects.
Ninth x bits for the third band of objects.

Puts objects 0-4 on sprites 3-7 for the top band of the screen: colour ($C11D), position ($C14A/$C14B), pointer ($C16A, into both screens' pointer bytes) for each active one, then the band's x-high, multicolour, priority and double-height bits ($C00A, $C000, $C003, $C006), with Clyde's and the shots' bits ($1286, $1218) added. Called from the raster chain.

The same for objects 5-9 in the middle band (tables from $C122, $C154, $C16F, $C251, and $C001, $C004, $C007, $C00B).
The same for objects 10-14 in the lowest band (tables from $C127, $C15E, $C174, $C256, and $C002, $C005, $C008, $C00C).
A value from each object's record (byte 15, high nibble), saved and cleared while the object flashes after a hit and restored afterwards; level_colours_next reads it ($268C).
Where object_flash_one keeps $C0FF during the flash, for object_colours to restore.
Each object's sprite colour, written to $D02A+ for its sprite by sprites_band1-3; set from record byte 4 or its colour cycle, and turned white during a hit flash.
Object 5's colour: sprites_band2 reads the colours of objects 5-9 from here.
Object 10's colour: sprites_band3 reads the colours of objects 10-14 from here.
$FF when the object is not flashing; during a hit flash its saved colour, restored by object_colours.
Frames left of each object's hit flash (2 at the start), counted down by object_colours.
The objects' sprite positions, x and y for each, copied from obj_xy each frame by objects_save_positions and read by the sprite bands.
The y byte of object 0's sprite position (x and y alternate from $C14A).
Sprite position of object 5, where sprites_band2 starts reading.
The y byte of object 5's sprite position.
Sprite position of object 10, where sprites_band3 starts reading.
The y byte of object 10's sprite position.

Each object's sprite frame (its sprite pointer), set by its animation script and written to both screens' pointer bytes by the sprite bands. The engine tells objects apart by it, and $0F, a blank sprite, marks a slot that is empty or removed.
Object 5's sprite frame, read by sprites_band2.
Object 10's sprite frame, read by sprites_band3.
Each object's score value (record byte 10, low nibble), used by score_add.
Loop count of each object's x movement script, for a loop command (a byte with bit 6 set).
Loop count of each object's y movement script.
The last step each object's x movement script made.
The last step each object's y movement script made.
Each object's state: 0 alive, 3 or more dying (object_kill sets 5 and counts down to 4 or 3 by its death type), 5 also for a removed object.
What a shot does to each object besides damage (record byte 7, bits 0-5), read by shot_hit_object.
The value obj_hits restarts from once the hit threshold is reached: 0, or $FF (record byte 8, bit 7) for a response that happens only once.
Each object's hit points, from the level's table at $8EAF; $FF makes it unharmed by shots.
Damage counted towards the hit threshold obj_hit_need; $FF once a one-off response has happened.
The damage after which an object's hit response runs (from the level's table at $8EDF by record byte 15).
Record byte 13 for each object: the item flag it clears in items_taken when collected, or the slot of the object it rides on (ride_parent).

Each object's wake delay, from the level's table at $8EBF by its record's byte 9 (object_spawn). An object spawned with a delay starts asleep (obj_awake clear) and objects_scroll counts the delay down once a frame, waking it when the count passes zero. $FE wakes it only when the scroll passes the level's end (scroll_column at $2705); $FF never.

Nonzero once the object is awake: set at once by object_spawn when its wake delay is 0, else by objects_scroll or scroll_column. A sleeping object neither moves nor animates (move_objects, animate_objects), cannot be hit (object_collisions) and its colour cycle waits (object_colours).
1 while each object's sprite is to be drawn; cleared when it is removed.
Object 5's shown flag, read by sprites_band2.
Object 10's shown flag, read by sprites_band3.
The ninth bit of each object's x position, five objects to a byte (bits 3-7) for the three bands; the fourth byte is cleared too.
The third band's x high bits (objects 10-14); objects_scroll also reads it at $1D5C.
Each object's position, x and y in turn for the 15 objects (y at $C260); the movement scripts and objects_scroll change it.
The y byte of object 0's position (x and y alternate from $C25F).
Cleared with the positions by objects_clear ($C6AE).
Low byte of each object's y movement script address (from the level's table at $8E6F).
High byte of each object's y movement script address (from $8E8F); 0 for none.
Low byte of each object's animation script address (the level's table $8D5A by type).
High byte of each object's animation script address ($8D92).
Low byte of each object's colour cycle list (the level's table $8E02).
High byte of each object's colour cycle list ($8E11).
The x movement script an object takes when it dies (record byte 0, high nibble).
The y movement script an object takes when it dies (record byte 10, high nibble).
The x movement script a hit switches the object to (record byte 12), cleared once used.
The y movement script a hit switches the object to (record byte 13), cleared once used.
The type a hit switches the object to (record byte 14), cleared once used.
Animation steps to skip, set to 2 by hit response $2A.

Steps the y movement script may still take, as obj_x_steps (hit response $30 adds one).
Frames before each object starts to move and animate, from the level's table at $8ECF.
Whether each object's animation runs: 1 freely, 0 not at all, $FF for one more pass (an object that animates when hit).
1 while the object's colour cycles through its list.
1 while the object's x movement script runs; some start at 0 until a hit starts them.
1 while the object's y movement script runs.
How each object moves with the landscape (record byte 8 bits 2-3: $01, $81 or $C1), read by objects_scroll.
Each object's linked group (record byte 8 bits 4-6): objects of a group die together and flash together.
The top two bits of record byte 3; kill_attacker reads them for riding objects.
Frames to the next animation step, reloaded from obj_anim_speed.
Frames between animation steps (the level's table at $8DCA by type).
Loop count for an animation script's loop command.
Where the animation script carries on after a loop.
Frames to the next colour of the object's colour cycle.
Frames between colours of the cycle (the level's table at $8E20).
Loop count for a colour list's loop command.
Where the colour list carries on after a loop.

For an object that rides on another (record byte 12 = $FE), the offsets from its parent (record byte 14); 0 otherwise.

Runs each object's two movement scripts, x then y (objects 14 down to 0). An object moves while it is alive, active, not dying, its start delay ($C351) and pause ($C324) are over and the script is on ($C37E, $C38D) with steps left ($C333, $C342). Script bytes: 0 holds still for the frame; $01-$0F move right (x) or down (y) by that many pixels (a larger value one pixel more, from the compare's carry); $80-$BF move left or up by the low nibble; $40-$7F and $C0-$FD loop back (count in the low six bits, distance in the next byte); $10 restarts the script (and repositions a riding object, ride_parent); $FE stops it; $FF plays the sound effect in the next byte (when the music is off). The x script carries into the ninth x bit. An object whose x reaches 200-219 while its x high bit is set has left the screen at the right and is removed with its group.
Operand of the LDY at $C4E5, written at $C4D8 with the script position of the sound command, restored after the sound request.
Operand of the LDX at $C4E7, written at $C4CF with the object slot, restored after the sound request.
Operand of the SBC at $C529, written with the x script's loop distance, which moves the read position back.
Operand of the LDX at $C5AC, written at $C59B with the slot of the object leaving, restored after its group is removed.
Removes object X at once: shows the blank sprite $0F, sets state 5 and clears its active and shown flags.
The y half of move_objects for object $39, from its y script ($C27F/$C28E, position $020F), with the same commands; sound effects come through definition $FFD4.
Operand of the LDY at $C61F, written at $C612: the y script position saved over the sound request.
Operand of the LDX at $C621, written at $C609: the object slot saved over the sound request.
Operand of the SBC at $C663, written with the y script's loop distance.
Empties all 15 object slots: blank sprite, positions, state, active flags and loop counts cleared.
objects_clear, then the four x high-bit bytes ($C25B) cleared. Called at each stage start.

Puts object X on the object it rides (slot obj_record_ref), offset by obj_ride: the low nibble picks an x offset from the level's table at $8EFC (bit 3 = to the left), bits 4-6 a y offset from $8F04 (bit 7 = upwards); the ninth x bit follows.

Steps the objects' animation scripts, the even slots one frame and the odd slots the next (the BEQ at $C769 is turned into BNE and back). An object animates while active, not removed (state 5 shows the blank sprite), its start delay and pause are over, it is alive and its animation is on ($C360). Every obj_anim_speed frames it reads the next byte of its script: a sprite frame, which becomes obj_frame; 0, which restarts the script; 1, which removes the object; or $40-$7F, a loop (count in the low six bits, distance back in the next byte).
The BEQ (or BNE) that picks even or odd slots; animate_objects flips its opcode after each pass.

Ends finished hit flashes (restoring colour and $C0FF when obj_flash_time runs out) and steps the colour cycles of half the objects each frame, alternating by the BEQ/BNE at $C843: every obj_cycle_speed frames the next byte of the object's colour list, a colour below $10, a restart at $10, or a loop with bit 6 set.
The BEQ (or BNE) that picks even or odd slots for the colour cycles; flipped after each pass.

The drive code: 256 bytes that fast_loader uploads to the 1541's $0700-$07FF (memory_swap 0 first exchanges this page with $4000, where the loader reads it) and starts at $07AB, here $F2AB. That entry takes the track and sector of the file's first block from $18/$19, where the KERNAL's OPEN left them, and queues the code at $0700 as a job ($E0) on buffer 4. The job reads each block into the drive's buffer at $0600 (DOS ROM routines $F50A and $F8E0), checks its header and checksum, and sends its bytes two bits at a time through the serial port at $1800, then follows the block's link to the next track and sector until the last block.

Shows the loading screen and loads the stage, entered from stage_next. Acknowledges and turns off the raster interrupt. For stage 1 it draws nothing and only sets up the load ($F889): the title is still on the screen. Otherwise it blanks the screen, turns the sprites off, fills the screen with character $FC in colour 11, selects the character set at $5000 and multicolour, and brings the loading screen's character set from $D000 to $5000 with three exchanges (memory_swap 6, 4 and 6 again, keeping $5800 as it was) and the drive code to $4000 (memory_swap 0). Before stage 2 it also exchanges $9A00 and $E000 (memory_swap 8), so that level 1.1's $9A00-$ABFF sits at $E000 while LB loads over it, and loader_hand_over can swap it back. It then draws the top and bottom bands, prints "LOADING" and the stage (or "GAME OVER" when the lives byte has gone negative) in red, shuts the weapons tablet and sets the background to yellow ($D021 = 7) and the border and multicolour 1 to light blue ($D020 and $D022 = $0E).
